007d6f6b-4f84-5cd4-97d4-b1637e409355.name: Emigrant family
007d6f6b-4f84-5cd4-97d4-b1637e409355.short_description: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. This photo belongs to a Turkish family who migrated from Crete to Turkey in 1925.
007d6f6b-4f84-5cd4-97d4-b1637e409355.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
keywords: migration; population exchange

00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.name: The Hijaz Railway construction workers
00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.short_description: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the interruption of the construction works caused by the outbreak of World War I.
00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.dates: Late 19th century – begining of the 20th century

01425452-ab97-5882-bfb1-7f4f896ba157.name: Omar Pasha (1806–1871)
01425452-ab97-5882-bfb1-7f4f896ba157.short_description: Portrait of Omar Pasha. He was born in Croatia in 1806 near the Turkish-Hungarian border. In 1828 he deserted from the Austrian army and joined the Ottoman administration in Bosnia. After a long career in the Ottoman army, he became the military governor of Bucharest and commanded the Ottoman forces at the siege of Sevastopol in Crimea. In 1862 he suppressed an uprising in Herzogovina and led a victorious campaign against Montenegro. In 1868 he became War Minister and died in 1871 in Istanbul.
keywords: Omar Pasha; Croatia; Bosnia; Ottoman empire; Herzegovina

01a64f5c-ceca-5e43-b3af-115b31492d64.name: Portrait of Abraham Salamon De Camondo
01a64f5c-ceca-5e43-b3af-115b31492d64.short_description: The Camondo Family is a family of Spanish-Portuguese Jewish origin. Abraham Salomon Camondo, who was born in İstanbul in 1781, acted as the Ottoman government's banker before the establishment of the Ottoman Bank. He founded a bank called "*Isaac et Compagnie Camondo*" with his brother Isaac in 1815. The bank grew in a short time period into a reputable international financial institution. Camondo prospered greatly and became the prime banker to the Ottoman Empire until the founding of the Imperial Ottoman Bank in 1863. The bank had a close relationship with the business community and banks of London, Paris and the Vienna Stock Exchange. The bank had also funded defence needs of Ottoman Empire during the Crimean War.
01a64f5c-ceca-5e43-b3af-115b31492d64.holder: The Quincentennial Foundation Museum, Zulfaris Synagogue Museum

01a88113-685d-5186-bbb9-828a46816c90.name: Portrait decoration
01a88113-685d-5186-bbb9-828a46816c90.short_description: This medallion featuring a portrait of the Shah is the highest Persian decoration; it was only presented to allied sovereigns and sometimes to other members of ruling dynasties. When the Shah visited Vienna for the World Fair in AD 1873 he presented it to the then 15-year-old Crown Prince Rudolf.

02c575a0-6154-582b-a588-2ae094079d0d.name: *Calligrapher Rıfat Efendi*
02c575a0-6154-582b-a588-2ae094079d0d.short_description: Feyhaman Duran was particularly interested in portrait painting and went to Paris in 1910 through the patronage of the Egyptian Prince Abbas Halim Pasha to further his studies in this genre. He greatly profited from the teaching of Paul Richet, professor of anatomy in the School of Fine Arts in Paris. He also attended the Julian Academy where he learned a great deal from Jean-Paul and Albert Laurens. In 1913-14 he worked in the Cormon studio in the School of Fine Arts. Although devoting most of his time to portrait painting, Feyhaman Duran also did paintings of flowers and nudes, but he was definitely most interested in the portrayal of people, and he had very little time for non-figurative painting.
keywords: Painting; Feyhaman Duran; orientalist painters

036f240e-d388-502f-b085-dcd2a8068418.name: Rashid Pasha Mustafa Mehmet (1802–1858)
036f240e-d388-502f-b085-dcd2a8068418.short_description: Portrait of Rashid Pasha. He was born in 1800 in Istanbul and joined the Ministry of Foreign Affairs at the age of 20. He served as Ottoman Ambassador in Paris and London. In 1837 he became Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Ottoman Empire. In 1838 he lost his position, but still negotiated as a Turkish diplomat in London, Paris and Berlin. In 1846 he became Grand Vizier and initiated a number of reforms.

03762b34-622e-5cca-85b2-11ca849dd5d2.name: The Hijaz Railway delegations
03762b34-622e-5cca-85b2-11ca849dd5d2.short_description: The Hijaz Railway ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj annual pilgrimage. Another important reason was to improve the economic and political integration of the distant Arabian provinces into the Ottoman state, and to facilitate the transportation of military forces.

059dc6e6-50b6-57db-9d8b-cf35da18b989.name: Pitcher
059dc6e6-50b6-57db-9d8b-cf35da18b989.description:
A massive pitcher made of blue cast glass with handle. The entire object is covered with decoration made according to designs of Czech artist Vladislav Titelbah (1847-1925). The image of a Serbian medieval ruler from the Nemanjić dynasty, Stefan the First Crowned, is centred under the pitcher's pour spout. Ornamentation designed by Vladislav Titelbah, a Czech born artist encircles the open rim and base.  
Vladislav Titelbah's opus contains over 9,000 watercolours, drawings, sketches and graphics inspired by Serbian folklore, national and mythology themes. He depicted rural interiors, persons, and scenes. During the 19th century, at the time of Serbian national awakening, his work had an important role. Today, his works are classified as first-class sources for the interpretation of Serbian visual culture and art of the 19th and the beginning of the 20th century.

06623ef3-6331-5463-b5c0-79f3249d4f5d.name: Painting of Ahmed Pacha Bey
06623ef3-6331-5463-b5c0-79f3249d4f5d.short_description: This oil on canvas portrait by the Swiss artist Charles Gleyre (1806–1874) depicts Ahmed Pacha Bey, the ruling prince of Tunisia at the time (1837–1855). He is dressed in official uniform, with red trousers with a gold strip and a black overcoat with gold epaulets, and is wearing the *muchir*'s insignia round his neck, and the Ordre du Sang, the Nichan al-Dam, and the Grand Croix de la Légion d'Honneur medals on the left of his chest. His torso his divided in two by a shimmering red sash of honour, his black and gold sword hangs off his belt on the left-hand side, and he is wearing a red chechia on his head. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

08086d2e-5ac6-53f2-810f-71dc4434785f.name: Portrait of the young dervish Nur 'Ali Shah (ca. 1748-1798)
08086d2e-5ac6-53f2-810f-71dc4434785f.short_description:
Half a century after his death, the dervish Nur ʿAli Shah (Hegira ca. 1161-1212 / AD ca. 1748-1798) enjoyed great popularity in Persia. Countless carpets from Kerman as well as various miniatures and oil portraits bear witness to this. It seems that this popularity was closely connected with the revival of Sufi traditions in the 19th century. All the portraits known so far can be traced back to two portraits painted by Ismaʿil Jalayer (d. Hegira 1284-1289 / AD 1868-1873) around 1865.  
  
The leaf originally belonged to an album made for Dr. Joseph Désiré Tholozon (Hegira 1235-1315 / AD 1820-1897) who was Nasir al-Din Shahʼs (r. Hegira 1264-1313 / AD 1848-1896) personal physician. He might have received the album from the shah in 1889 when he retired. This folio bears the number 50 and must have been the last leaf of his album, which itself was taken apart and probably sold in the early 20th century. Individual leaves formerly belonged to the collection of Jean Pozzi and are now in the Musée dʼArt et dʼHistoire in Geneva (Switzerland).
08086d2e-5ac6-53f2-810f-71dc4434785f.initial_owner: Joseph Désiré Tholozan (1820-1897); 1920s: Salomon Family, Paris; 1990s-ca. 1994: private collection, Paris; ca. 1995-2013: private collection, Belgium
08086d2e-5ac6-53f2-810f-71dc4434785f.method_for_datation: By comparison with similar dated works.
08086d2e-5ac6-53f2-810f-71dc4434785f.method_for_provenance: By comparison with objects that once belonged to Joseph Désiré Tholozan that are now in the Musée dʼart et dʼhistoire in Geneva, Switzerland. Information of previous owners was provided by the gallery, where the object was bought in 2013.
08086d2e-5ac6-53f2-810f-71dc4434785f.obtention: Acquisition with funds of Regula Brunner-Vontobel

08086d2e-5ac6-53f2-810f-71dc4434785f.author: Axel Langer
materials: Opaque watercolour and gold on paper

0b6eceea-2f90-5eb6-9483-03f0734b34dc.name: Misrata [Libya]. In the Home of Gabrielli, Agent of the Society of Maritime Services [Società dei servizi marittimi]
0b6eceea-2f90-5eb6-9483-03f0734b34dc.short_description:
In 19th and early 20th century Africa, the nature of the relations between European men and African women varied dramatically according to the different power relations between the partners. In colonial situations, the legal subordination of the colonised people put African women in particularly weak positions vis-à-vis European men, generally resulting in very exploitative relationships. In countries that were not under European rule, more balanced relationships could develop.  
This picture shows a mixed family in Libya before the onset of Italian colonialism. The setting of the picture suggests that the Libyan woman enjoyed respect and status within the family: the woman and her children are sitting on chairs, surrounded by persons who appear to be domestic servants, and the Italian man is standing behind her, looking at their children.
0b6eceea-2f90-5eb6-9483-03f0734b34dc.author: Patrizia Pampana, Giulia Barrera

0cd36a65-5e7b-5bb2-8525-edcaea12dea2.name: Omar al-Mukhtar (1861–1931), leader of anticolonial resistance in Libya
0cd36a65-5e7b-5bb2-8525-edcaea12dea2.short_description:
In 1923, the head of the Senussi Muslim order Mohamed Idris charged Omar al-Mukhtār (1861-1931) with the task of leading Libyan anti-colonial resistance. Omar al-Mukhtār was leader of the Libyan anti-Italian guerrillas, until he was captured and executed by the Italians in 1931.  
In 1911-12, Italy successfully waged war against Turkey for the colonial conquest of Libya. However, during WWI Italy lost control of most of the Libyan territory. After the war, it took Italy about ten years to re-establish its hold on Libyan inland areas.  
Thanks to his military genius, to the wide popular support he enjoyed and the financial help provided by the Senussia, Omar al-Mukhtār was able to keep the Italians in check for years, even when the army of the invaders was ten times larger than the guerrilla forces. The Italians were able to capture him only after deporting part of the population of the Cyrenaica mountains (Gebel Akhda) in concentration camps on the coast.
0cd36a65-5e7b-5bb2-8525-edcaea12dea2.author: Giulia Barrera

0cdaaac9-facc-525a-b1f1-756e4b6df842.name: Silvio Benigno Crespi and his family in the courtyard of Villa Pia (Villa Crespi), Orta San Giulio (Novara)
0cdaaac9-facc-525a-b1f1-756e4b6df842.short_description:
Silvio Benigno Crespi was one of the children of Cristoforo Benigno Crespi, the industrialist who built a Moorish-style villa (known as villa Pia or villa Crespi) built on the lake d’Orta.  
This picture was taken in the courtyard of Villa Crespi. It shows Silvio Benigno Crespi (standing, on the right); sitting on the extreme left is his wife Teresa Ghiglieri; at the centre their first-born child Benigno and their other six children.  
The picture gives a hint of the lifestyle of this stock of cultivated, enlightened and successful industrialists.
0cdaaac9-facc-525a-b1f1-756e4b6df842.author: Ignazio Galella

0d5820f1-3545-5a87-813f-427001d4dd48.name: *Eliza Bedeković* née *Novak*
0d5820f1-3545-5a87-813f-427001d4dd48.description:
Baroness Bedeković (d. about 1850) married Franjo Bedeković Komorski (1755–1827), a prominent figure in Croatian political life, at the end of the 18th century or the beginning of the 19th century. Elected to the Lower House of the Hungarian-Croatian parliament in Buda in 1790, by 1808 Bedeković was Administrator of Križevci County and, from 1809 to 1825, Grand Sheriff of Bekeš County. From 1825 to his death, he was Grand Sheriff of Križevci County. During his many terms in office, he was a noted Croatian patriot.  
This portrait, probably painted in Vienna at the end of the 18th century, is probably by Johann Baptist Lampi the Elder. Lampi had returned to Vienna from St. Petersburg in around 1797, the year this portrait was finished. Lampi's portraits of this period show meticulous attention to detail in the fine materials and jewellery – details of which abound in this portrait of Baroness Bedeković.
0d5820f1-3545-5a87-813f-427001d4dd48.short_description: This outstanding portrait of Baroness Bedeković – wife of Franjo Bedeković – is probably the work of Johann Baptist Lampi the Elder. Lampi’s portraits of this period show meticulous attention to detail in the fine materials and jewellery – details of which abound in this portrait.
0d5820f1-3545-5a87-813f-427001d4dd48.method_for_datation: The date and possible authorship of this painting were established by study of historical information on the Bedekovićs, stylistic analysis and comparison of other known works by J. B. Lampi the Elder.
0d5820f1-3545-5a87-813f-427001d4dd48.obtention: Bought for the Museum in 1900 from a private owner in Zagreb.

0e467a26-3229-554d-8707-115f086aa0be.name: Portrait of Claudius Rich
0e467a26-3229-554d-8707-115f086aa0be.short_description: Rich was the East India Company’s first Resident in Baghdad. He was a talented linguist. In his spare time he explored ancient sites, producing the first proper plans of Babylon and Nineveh. He hosted important travellers to Iraq, searching for sites of Biblical relevance. In 1821 he died during a cholera outbreak in Shiraz. His collection formed the nucleus of the British Museum’s collection.
keywords: Bible; travelling; archaeology; archaeological excavation; exploration; collecting; collector; museums

0e6e6bac-3e5d-5bc0-b143-7f8c186c37a6.name: A Portrait of a European, after Jacques de Gheyn's print 'Terra'
0e6e6bac-3e5d-5bc0-b143-7f8c186c37a6.short_description: This miniature painting depicted an image of a European soldier made by Mughal artist around 17th century. The original image is based on a European print by Dutch printmaker Jacques de Gheyn (1565–1629). This painting which is made with gouache on paper technique showing a European with fair skin colour in European style of clothes holding a long object, probably a weapon such as a spear or gun. At the margin of the painting inscribed the word ‘awwal’, possibly indicating the grade of the painting and at the back with Mughal seals impressions. The fondness to European prints was common in Mughal court. Emperors such as Akbar and later Jahangir were among the collectors of European prints.

10e20816-215a-59c8-b59d-b15f4c933e82.name: Mahmud II Sultan of Turkey (1784–1839)
10e20816-215a-59c8-b59d-b15f4c933e82.short_description:
Portrait of Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey (1784–1839). In 1826 Mahmud II initiated the development of a modern army. This led to the uprising of the Janissary, which was quelled by massacring the rebellious troops. Under Mahmud II's reign, in 1821 the Greeks started their fight for freedom which was granted to them in the Peace of Adrianople in 1829.  
After the destruction of the Janissary, the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Mahmud II had only 35,000 badly trained regular soldiers in 1827. Due to the weakness of the Ottoman Empire, Ibrahim Pasha, the son of Muhammad 'Ali (ruler of Egypt), invaded Syria. On 20 February 1832, the Egyptian Army defeated the Ottoman Army at the Battle of Konya. This forced Mahmud II to sign the Peace of Kütahya and to cede Syria and Kilikia to Egypt.
keywords: Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Janissary; Konya; Ibrahim Pasha; Muhammad Ali; Greece

117f9344-faa8-5cdb-8423-bab797cf66a2.name: *Portrait of Paul V Borghese*
117f9344-faa8-5cdb-8423-bab797cf66a2.description:
The piece is signed on the left “MARCELLI PROVENZALIS CENTEN. OPUS” and has the inscription “PAVLVS. V. BURGHESIVS. ROMANVS. P. O. M. ANN. MDCXXI. PONT. XVI.” on the bottom. The mosaic was commissioned from the artist by Cardinal Scipione Borghese, nephew of the Pope. The meticulous fine-detail in the work, such as the fur trim on the *camauro* (a cap traditionally worn by the Pope) and the *mozzetta* (a short elbow length cape worn by Catholic clergy), is impressive. The expressive rendering combines the nature of the individual and the solemn pose in keeping with the position of successor to Peter in perfect equilibrium. The papal coat of arms of the Casa Borghese, recognisable by the eagle and the dragon, appears in the top right.  
The work is mentioned as extraordinary in the biography of Marcello Provenzale, and he was included amongst the greatest artists of his time by Giovanni Baglione in 1642. For his rare ability to produce mosaics with tiny tiles, usually done on cartoons prepared by important painters, Provenzale was deemed by his contemporaries to be greater than the masters of the classical age. During the pontificate of Paul V, he received numerous commissions for the Vatican Basilica, where he completed the mosaic for the Clementina Chapel using a design by Cristoforo Roncalli, also known as Pomarancio, and the ones in the cupola. He made extensive contributions to the restoration of the famous 14th-century Giotto mosaic the *Navicella*. He was one of the preferred artists of Scipione Borghese, who commissioned numerous works from him, many of which are kept today in the museum, and he lived as a *protégé* at the residence of the princely Roman family.
117f9344-faa8-5cdb-8423-bab797cf66a2.short_description: Portrait of the reigning Pope executed by a trusted artist of Cardinal Scipione Borghese, who lived in the cardinal’s palace as his protégé. The strong realism and the highly unusual and difficult technique, of which Provenzale was very proud, represent typically Baroque characteristics.
117f9344-faa8-5cdb-8423-bab797cf66a2.obtention: The Borghese Collection was acquired by the Italian State in 1902.

1313c11f-d35a-5fba-85ac-6b580ca2b754.name: Headdress ornament
1313c11f-d35a-5fba-85ac-6b580ca2b754.short_description: A headdress ornament with the portrait of Fath Ali Shah (1797-1834) in painted enamel. It is shaped as a half-shaped moon combined by the rising sun that was the emblem of the Persian order of honour founded by the Shah in 1807. The bejewelled imperial crown refers to later oil paintings of him, since in the early years of his reign he is usually portrayed in the traditional royal turban topped by an aigrette.
keywords: Headdress ornament; Iran; Fath Ali Shah; Gold; costume

14edc45d-6bf0-507b-a305-757f6f034ef5.name: Portrait of Emperor Shah Jahan
14edc45d-6bf0-507b-a305-757f6f034ef5.short_description: The bearded emperor Shah Jahan, with a nimbus around his head, stands facing proper left, holding a flower in his raised left hand, his right clasping the hilt of his sheathed sword, which is pointed toward the ground. He wears a *jama* (a kind of frock with skirt). A *kamarband* (sash with ends pendant) girdles the waist, and a *dupatta* (scarf) falls over the left shoulder, the end dropping to the waist line. A dagger (*kataar*) is stuck in his sash on his waist. On his feet are heelless slippers. *Pajamas* are worn under the *jama*. The emperor also wears a jeweled *pagari* (turban) with the *sarpes* (plume), encircled by a dark halo. The *sarpes* appears to be jeweled. He wears the following jewelry: a *mala* (necklace); a *bhuja* band (armlet); and a *kangana* (bracelet). A tannish-gold thin border with dark-tan floral drawings surrounds the painting. The page background is decorated in a floral motif with feral feline heads in shades of tan and gold.

161d25a6-f2f3-5bd7-9bce-84afb082e31e.name: The Hijaz Railway Delegations
161d25a6-f2f3-5bd7-9bce-84afb082e31e.short_description: The Hijaz Railway ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj annual pilgrimage. Another important reason was to improve the economic and political integration of the distant Arabian provinces into the Ottoman state, and to facilitate the transportation of military forces.

183b5543-14a1-5a82-b3dd-50b7597cdf96.name: *Father Martin Stredonius with a View of Brno from the East*
183b5543-14a1-5a82-b3dd-50b7597cdf96.description:
The scene glorifies the Jesuit priest and teacher Martin Středa (known as Stredonius, practicing in Gliwica in 1587; moving to Brno in 1649). Set in 1645, when the Swedish besieged the city of Brno during the Thirty Years' War, the painting depicts Středa's miraculous ascension to heaven at the very moment the attackers withdrew. The final and largest cannon ball aimed at Brno is said to have landed at Father Středa's feet where it remained, motionless. A besieger holding a cannon ball is shown in the bottom left-hand corner, while the focal point of the picture is the priest accepting holy wisdom through the Virgin Mary, expressed by a reflection of divine light. Středa is wearing a medallion with a portrait of the emperor, which accentuates his role as a defender not only of Brno but also of the whole Habsburg empire. In the top right-hand corner appear Jan Kapistrán (Capistranus) and another church father. Capistranus preached in Brno in 1451 and was also believed to possess supernatural powers. The *veduta* of Brno shows the fortified character of the city, with Špilberk castle.  
General Ludvík Raduit de Souches, commander of the Brno defense during the Swedish siege complies: “It appears that the bravery of the city defense was strengthened by fervent prayers and continuous fasting on the part of Father Středa, through which he transmuted power from heaven to defend and ensure the safety of the besieged. The enemy eventually saw that, having mobilised all their military efforts and set all kinds of traps, the spirit of the city was strong and unbreakable, and that it involved supernatural protection …”  Stredonius is said to have had the power of being in two places at once and of levitating during meditation. He wrote a biography of the martyred priest Jan Sarkander, a document that played a major part in the dissemination of the latter's cult and eventual canonisation as patron saint of Moravia and counterpart to St. John of Nepomuk.  
The cult of Martin Středa was promoted through prints of a similar composition. (Brno City Archive).
183b5543-14a1-5a82-b3dd-50b7597cdf96.short_description: The scene glorifies the Jesuit priest Martin Středa. It is set in 1645, when the Swedish besieged the city of Brno during the Thirty Years' War, depicting Středa's miraculous ascension to heaven at the very moment that the attackers withdrew. The *veduta* shows the fortified character of the city of Brno.
183b5543-14a1-5a82-b3dd-50b7597cdf96.method_for_datation: The picture is thought to have been commissioned by the Brno Jesuit Václav Škodovský. The authorship, originally ascribed to M. Willman, was determined by Dr. Vlasta Kratinová, curator of the Moravian Gallery collections. Lublinský produced several paintings for Brno clients at the time, such as *The* *Allegory of Justice* (Old Brno Abbey) and *The Guardian Angel* for Count Dietrichstein (Church of St. Thomas).
183b5543-14a1-5a82-b3dd-50b7597cdf96.obtention: The picture was donated to the Brno Picture Gallery – which came into existence as part of the Francis Museum, Brno – by Provincial Councillor Franz Georg Eberle in 1821, shortly after its establishment. The painting also featured in the museum’s first exhibition held in the Episcopal courtyard.

When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This albumen portrait of Amelia del Valle y Serrano is delicate and quiet, with outstanding deep chocolate colour which reveals the quality of the photographic technique and the good condition of the object.

185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
185ba5fa-c953-5b73-a895-436fd368117e.short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

190def5c-0fc3-5e3c-8e0e-0783372b1471.name: Portrait of the Crown Prince Abbas Mirza (AH 1203–1248 / AD 1789–1833)
190def5c-0fc3-5e3c-8e0e-0783372b1471.short_description: This painting was originally conceived as architectural decoration, as it was intended to fill niches or partitions in royal palaces. It depicts two main themes; life size portraiture of Abbas Mirza and a battle scene. The portraits were characterised by their high level of details and bright palette (primarily pink, royal blue, turquoise and translucent green). Among the interesting feature of this painting is the background scene which shows a long line of troops standing against a forest background. The troops are depicted wearing European style costume; this reveals the importance of the modernization of the army of Abbas Mirza, which is a common theme in many Abbas Mirza’s portraits. However, one particular interest here is the single soldier looking directly at us, who is larger in size than the soldiers and thus of a more important status. It is believed that this soldier is a self-portrait of the artist who is believed to be Muhammad Hassan (Hegira 1233 / AD 1818).

198dcaff-0328-5a80-a4ea-d7ac0774b16b.name: *The Ancestral Gallery of the Eltz Family*
198dcaff-0328-5a80-a4ea-d7ac0774b16b.description:
The Eltz family were of ancient German nobility. They came originally from the town of Eltz in Moselland, their family lineage uninterrupted from the first decade of the 13th century. A branch of the counts of Eltz acquired estates in Slavonia in 1736, when Philipp Karl, archbishop and elected prince of Mainz, bought the Vukovar estate. Throughout the following decades, the family brought from Germany to Croatia family portraits and the *Ancestral Gallery*, consisting of 10 large paintings. The composition is the same for them all – four to six figures representing two generations of the family (father, mother, the eldest son and his wife) shown with the Eltz family's coats of arms combined with that of their wives. The lower areas of the paintings have long texts about the lives of those depicted. The elder generations of the family are sometimes dressed quite fantastically, while depictions of the later generations seen in the final painting in the Gallery (shown here) present a detailed study of the fashion of the period  
The *Gallery*, commissioned and painted during the second half of the 18th century, is probably the work of Georg Joseph Melber, a painter based in Mainz. In 1752, Melber painted portraits of Anselm Kasimir Eltz and his wife Maria Johanna (in the Gallery of Fine Arts in Osijek). These portraits are distinctly similar to the paintings of the Ancestral Gallery.
198dcaff-0328-5a80-a4ea-d7ac0774b16b.short_description: The Eltz family belonged to ancient German nobility. A branch of the counts of Eltz acquired estates in Slavonia in the 18th century bringing from Germany to Croatia the *Ancestral Gallery*. *The Gallery*, comprising 10 paintings, dates to the last quarter of the 18th century.
198dcaff-0328-5a80-a4ea-d7ac0774b16b.method_for_datation: The date and possible authorship of the painting was established by studying the inscriptions, and comparing the painting with other known works of Georg Joseph Melber.
198dcaff-0328-5a80-a4ea-d7ac0774b16b.obtention: Received from the Commission for the Collection and Preservation of Cultural Monuments and Antiquities in 1952.

*Od svagdana do blagdana. Barok u Hrvatskoj. Katalog izložbe* (From Everyday to Holidays: Baroque in Croatia), exhibition catalogue, Zagreb, 1993, p. 248.
198dcaff-0328-5a80-a4ea-d7ac0774b16b.author: Marina Bregovac Pisk
keywords: Ancestral gallery; portrait; Eltz family; heraldry; coat of arms; fashion

19adb7d5-92bf-5c8a-8b63-f8d677d0e713.short_description: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro (1871–1939) was the eldest son of King Nicola I of Montenegro. 1a28e275-5d29-5396-afed-1d35fe8bd656.short_description: This impressive three-quarter-profile portrait of Ibrahim Adil Shah at about 19 years of age is a unique masterpiece in every way. 1c651cdc-3180-5289-952f-daeae5e69f65.short_description: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. This photo depicts some Muslim migrants who immigrated to America.

1c78b924-ed6f-5a33-8922-4aa69a219c71.name: Portraits of Jahangir and Shah Jahan
1c78b924-ed6f-5a33-8922-4aa69a219c71.short_description: This album painting shows portraits of two Mughal emperors; the upper portrait shows Jahangir (r. 1605–27) in a *jharoka* window-scene, while the lower, larger portrait depicts his son, Shah Jahan (r. 1627–58) in greater dimensions, a golden nimbus or halo encircling his head. Most famous today for commissioning the Taj Mahal, Shah Jahan was also a connoisseur of gemstones. In this portrait, he is richly adorned with necklaces, bracelets, and pendants of pearls, emeralds, rubies, and other jewels. He wears an orange turban decorated with strings of pearls, rubies, and emeralds and a sapphire turban-ornament (*sarpech*) of black aigrette feathers. His gold belt glitters with diamonds and a large opal. In his sash is tucked a dagger or *katar*, and his right arm leans on a sword. He is holding his imperial seal on his left hand, a sign of his sovereignty.

1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.name: Types of Cairo
1c7eb8dd-c27a-55e4-b4bd-256860c07387.short_description: The historical photos, belonging to Enrico H. Giglioli's collection, were collected by the Florentine naturalist during his travel around the world in 1865–68 on the Magenta's steam corvette, with the purpose to start diplomatic and commercial relations. The "genre" images seem to be created "ad hoc" to represent human diversity along the different ages. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum, and are very important for the history of anthropological science and history of photography. The origins in terms of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

1deb708b-ab5d-5f99-8702-421204b044cf.name: Berber woman (Nailiya) lying down
1deb708b-ab5d-5f99-8702-421204b044cf.description: The image depicts a Nailiya, a woman of the Berber tribe of the Ouled Naïl, in the south of Algeria. She is lying on her side like an odalisque, wearing a colourful silk dress and the rich jewels used to perform their traditional dance. The Nailiyat were independent women, free to marry men of their choosing. They moved to the cities in the North to earn money as dancers, in order to maintain their families in their community of origin. All this was not fully understood by Europeans. With the emergence of sex-tourism these women were forced to introduce sexual content in their originally hieratic performance, and finally they were even considered as prostitutes by the French administration, which in turn led to them being repudiated in their villages. Early photography contributed to forge this image of the Nailiyat in the European imagination.
keywords: Photography; Orientalism; Algeria; Women

1e2c6043-b6b2-543a-9e30-6ef03d18caa0.description: The *Portrait of Baron Ferdinand Laffert* mixes official characteristics with a more personal style. The Baron was among the newcomers that gained estates after the Turks were ousted from Hungarian soil, and became the new landlord of a settlement in Ócsa, in Pest county near Buda, Hungary in 1693. He published one work during his lifetime, the *Publicus installationis actus in s. regni Hungariae coronae conservatorem excell., ac illustr. dni. comitis Georgii Leopoldi Erdődy de Monyorókerék ... Anno ab InItIo regnI HVungarIae, Ita & eXorDIo saCrae Coronae, Svpra septIngentos trIgesIMo. Posonii* in 1730.

1f4778d6-1457-56dc-8745-6fecef3643f8.short_description: Portrait of Huseyn Avni Pasha, who was murdered in 1876 by Hasan Bey. In 1874 Huseyn Avni Pasha became Grand Vizier. 2014af0a-f0bc-59a2-9a32-22eb77035668.name: Ferdinand I, Czar of Bulgaria (1861–1948)
2014af0a-f0bc-59a2-9a32-22eb77035668.short_description: Portrait of Ferdinand I (1861–1948) as Duke of Bulgaria. Ferdinand I was born as the son of the Austrian General August von Sachsen-Coburg and Gotha. In 1887 he became ruler of Bulgaria after the abdication of Alexander I von Battenberg. In 1908 he made himself Tsar of Bulgaria. Because he joined the German and Austrian monarchy in WWI and lost the war, he had to abdicate on 3 October 1918 and to emigrate to Germany and Slovakia. In 1948 Ferdinand I of Bulgaria died in Coburg, Germany.

20742252-5d4f-565f-8b1e-0849b9510ddd.short_description: Portrait of Abdul-Mejid I, Sultan of Turkey (1823–1861). When he came to power in 1839, he tried to re-occupy lands lost to Muhammad 'Ali, the ruler of Egypt. In this effort he was supported by Britain and Austria. In 1840 a combined British-Austrian fleet cut off the supply lines of the Egyptian army and forced the Egyptians to sign the 1840 Convention of Alexandria. Abdul-Mejid was able to win back Syria and Palestine. In 1849 he granted the Hungarian refugees exile. In 1861 he died and left his throne to his brother Abdülaziz.

21983581-bf0c-5102-8ca7-8f1af359caf4.short_description: Portrait of Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892). After the deposition of his father Ismail Pasha, Muhammad Tawfiq took over the government in Egypt. The Arabi revolution diminished his power radically. In 1882 he asked for help from Great Britain. British troops suppressed the Arabi revolution and occupied Egypt. Muhammad Tawfiq became ruler at the grace of the British government.

21d2fd52-ed06-5897-a1ce-fe2e55d7e878.name: *Sultan Süleyman II in profile*
21d2fd52-ed06-5897-a1ce-fe2e55d7e878.short_description: This portrait of the Ottoman Sultan Süleyman (AD 1494/5– 1566) is generally attributed to Titian’s circle, mainly because of the inscription on the back of the painting. No original portrait of Süleyman by Titian has survived, but inventories document four portraits by him, among them two tentatively identified as portraits in profile. Comparison with other recorded portrait-types of Süleyman shows that its genesis is connected with a prototype disseminated by Paolo Giovio (AD 1483–1552) after AD 1543, when he commissioned a number of copies of portraits of sultans for his portrait collection at Como. This year marks the *terminus post quem* for this painting.
21d2fd52-ed06-5897-a1ce-fe2e55d7e878.method_for_datation: Inscription on the back of the painting "Tiziano" and stilistical analysis as well as historical context.
21d2fd52-ed06-5897-a1ce-fe2e55d7e878.method_for_provenance: The painting is recorded in the Inventory of the Imperial Gallery dated AD 1772 (number 130): "Ein Türcken Kopf". Probably the same painting recorded in the inventory of the collection of Archduke Ferdinand II of Tirol AD 1596.

21fbb370-0706-50de-a10a-ae6eb3f6cb65.short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

2398d928-c319-50b3-8b82-b2185dea28d6.short_description: Lady Layard, wife of the famous excavator of Assyria, Austen Henry Layard, here poses in ‘Assyrian’ jewellery. This was made for her using genuine ancient objects.

25615117-b95e-51bc-bba3-33731c28624f.name: Portrait of a young woman
25615117-b95e-51bc-bba3-33731c28624f.description: A young woman on the photograph poses in the interior, lying on the Pirot kilim. She is wearing an overcoat named *džube*, which belongs to traditional urban dress ensemble worn in Kosovo. For this occasion *džube* is turned into an evening dress and combined with modern accessories. The outfit was most probably worn at a costume ball, which was a popular practice at this time, related to the elements of traditional 19th century urban dress. The kilim on the photo is decorated with the *Crown Prince* (*prestolonaslednik*) ornament.
25615117-b95e-51bc-bba3-33731c28624f.author: Draginja Maskareli
keywords: Pirot; Şarköy; kilim; photograph

261e731d-c1f3-5549-9d76-8e6eb76876e3.name: Alexander I Obrenovic, King of Serbia (1876–1903)
261e731d-c1f3-5549-9d76-8e6eb76876e3.short_description: Portrait of Alexander I Obrenovic, King of Serbia (1876–1903) as a young man. Between the abdication of his father in 1889 and his proclamation as a king in 1893, his mother Natalija Obrenovic ruled as a regent. Being a close ally of Austria, he became Serbian King in 1893. In 1894 Alexander abolished the liberal constitution of Serbia. In 1900 he married Draga Masin, a former lady-in-waiting of his mother. This marriage was very unpopular and weakened the political position of the king. In 1903 he and his wife were murdered by a group of Serbian officers.

26e9ef4b-0b68-5435-8e38-53a259f9cdaf.name: Portrait of Prosper Enfantin dressed in an imitation of the local style
26e9ef4b-0b68-5435-8e38-53a259f9cdaf.short_description: Prosper Enfantin (1796–1864) was one of the most active members of the Saint-Simonian movement (a socio-economic and political movement advocating a fraternal, socialist society based on economic prosperity). After being imprisoned in 1832 for founding a very politically-active community, Enfantin became fascinated by the Middle East, and in 1834 he left for Egypt with a few companions. He was also one of the proponents of the Suez Canal. In this image he is dressed in the local Egyptian style, wearing clothes he made himself.
keywords: Saint-Simonianism; Prosper Enfantin

275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.short_description: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).
275443d0-1d7d-5e19-a7ef-50820f9add5d.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling

27da4fd7-996d-5066-b357-ffc4082c83ad.short_description: This is a photograph of the Nobel Prize for Medicine won by Dr Charles Nicolle for his work on infectious illnesses during his time at l'Institut Pasteur from 1903 to 1936.

2cba4816-822e-5153-8c2f-a05c21e94c01.short_description: Portrait of Mulay 'Abd al-Rahman, Sultan of Morocco (1789–1859). 2efb58fe-14fe-59df-ad70-18b84374d4f5.name: Edmund Count Szechenyi (1839–1922)
2efb58fe-14fe-59df-ad70-18b84374d4f5.short_description: Portrait of Count Edmund Szechenyi. He was born in 1839 in Bratislava and studied the work of fire brigades in London. In 1869 he founded in Budapest the first volunteer fire brigade, which was transformed into a professional fire brigade in 1870. From 1871–1874 he commanded the umbrella organisation of all fire brigades in Hungary. In 1875 he was sent by Emperor Franz Joseph to Istanbul to build up a fire brigade in the Ottoman capital. As head of the fire brigade he became the first Christian Pasha in the Ottoman Army and stayed in Istanbul until his death in 1922.

2f2d6f96-e497-5489-ae20-7c7ca9950d9b.name: *Mulay Hassan, Sultan of Tunis, died 1550*
2f2d6f96-e497-5489-ae20-7c7ca9950d9b.short_description:
This portrait of Mulay Hassan, the Sultan of Tunis, is based on either a painting in the Uffizi Galleries or its now-lost prototype that was once in the collection of portraits assembled by Paolo Giovio. All of the portraits in the collection seem to be based on a portrait of the sultan by Cornelisz Vermeyen, the Netherlandish artist who had accompanied Charles V on his Tunisian campaign in AD 1535. The latter was the emperor’s response to the capture of the city by the Ottoman admiral, Hayreddin Barbarossa, which had forced the emperor’s ally, Mulay Hassan, to flee to Spain.  
From the collection of more than 900 portraits that Archduke Ferdinand II of Tyrol (AD 1529–95) began to assemble in AD 1676. The small paintings come from a variety of sources and depict both famous historical and contemporary personalities.

His reign marked a final cultural flowering in Egypt, which coincided with its growing conflicts with the Ottoman Empire. This portrait is probably based on a now-lost prototype once in the collection of Paolo Giovio, which also served as the model for a painting now in the Uffizi Galleries and a woodcut by Tobias Stimmer.

316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.name: *Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey* (painting)
316c3ae7-9ea6-5cac-b035-f8104f24c1ed.short_description: This 1861 oil on canvas by B. de Moynier shows the Mohamed Sadok Pacha Bey in front of the throne in the great hall of the Palais du Bardo, his right hand on the Tunisian constitution (which he has just proclaimed), his left holding his sword. He is dressed in official uniform, with red trousers with a gold stripe and a short black coat with a gold belt and epaulets, in addition to the Nichan al-Amen medal and a green sash with a double red stripe. On his chest the Nichan al-Dam, the Légion d'Honneur and the Nichan al-Iftikhar (classe majeur) medals can be seen, as well as a Légion d'Honneur and Nichan al-Iftikhar on a sling. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.

3277a1c4-6310-5adb-8af8-8874fed7d747.name: *Marija Terezija Oršić (nee Wintershofen)*
3277a1c4-6310-5adb-8af8-8874fed7d747.description:
By birth from a Styrian baronial family, Maria Theresia Wintershofen was extremely well educated. She married Count Antun Oršić (1670/6–1706), a descendant of an old Croatian baronial family who was a cavalry captain and first served in the War of Spanish Succession and then fought against the Turks in Hungary. Maria Theresia and Count Oršić married when they were both very young, before 1695. Soon after, in 1700, he sued her for adultery and for allegedly casting spells on him. Granted a divorce, he took away their three children.  
An unknown, probably Croatian painter has bestowed on this portrait of Maria Theresia something unusual and mysterious, somehow reflecting her strange destiny. The portrait magnificently illustrates various details of female aristocratic dress at the end of the 17th century, notably the influence of French fashion seen in the cap (*fontange)* which is highly decorative and made of ruffled white lace and red ribbons threaded with silver. The colourful dress she wears was typical of the 17th century, richly endowed with pearls and lace. She also wears a small watch, hung on a red ribbon from her waist, accentuating her high social position.

Maria Theresia and Count Oršić married when they were both very young, before 1695. Soon after, in 1700, he sued her for adultery and for allegedly casting spells on him. Granted a divorce, he took away their three children. The portrait magnificently portrays various details of female dress at the end of the 17th century.

33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.name: Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and Amelia del Valle y Serrano, in Oriental garment
33c78378-09b9-5e76-bb0d-85f0948fe81c.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, Marquise of Cerralbo, and her daughter Amelia del Valle y Serrano is delicious thanks to the typical Turkish costume, the apparently easy pose and the scenography and the absolute harmony with the idea of aesthetic orientalism.

keywords: Portrait; women; souvenir; memorabilia; orientalism

35b961a6-875c-5ccf-a80f-d6f917ccd48e.name: Jozef Zachariasz Bem (1795–1850)
35b961a6-875c-5ccf-a80f-d6f917ccd48e.short_description: Portrait of Jozef Zachariasz Bem as Turkish Pasha. Jozef Bem was born in the Austrian part of Poland. He fought as a Napoleonic officer against the Russians. In 1830 he participated in the Polish uprising against the Russians in Warsaw. In 1848 he was one of the leading Generals fighting with the Hungarian army against the Habsburg troops. After several defeats in 1849, he fled with 6,000 Hungarian-Polish soldiers to the Ottoman Empire. After converting to Islam, he became a Turkish General. In 1850 he suppressed an Arabic pogrom against the Christian population of Aleppo.
keywords: Jozef Zachariasz Bem; Aleppo; Syria; Hungary

3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.name: Photograph
3a9203b3-ee28-58a5-9738-28760f62fc9b.short_description:
This photograph is taken from a family photograph album. Most of the photographs in it are printed on platinum paper, which was introduced in 1879.  
Throughout most of the 19th century women had few legal rights to property, money, children, or even, after marriage, their own bodies. However, there were great changes in attitudes during the last decade of the century. The traditional role of women was questioned and some women openly defied convention. They educated themselves by reading widely and took up what were seen as 'un-ladylike' activities such as smoking and cycling. The free movement of the bicycle was seen as a symbol of equality and personal freedom.

3abe2459-c22d-5b5d-907a-4be0147c9eec.name: Seated Berber woman (Nailiya)
3abe2459-c22d-5b5d-907a-4be0147c9eec.description:
The image depicts a Nailiya, a woman of the Berber tribe of the Ouled Naïl, in the south of Algeria. She is sitting among rich cushions, wearing a colourful silk dress and the jewels used to perform their traditional dance.  
The Nailiyat were independent women, free to marry men of their choosing. They moved to the cities in the North to earn money as dancers, in order to maintain their families in their community of origin. All this was not fully understood by Europeans. With the emergence of sex tourism these women were forced to introduce sexual content in their originally hieratic performance, and finally they were even considered as prostitutes by the French administration, in turn leading to being repudiated in their villages.  
Early photography contributed to forge this image of the Nailiyat in the European imagination.
keywords: Photography; Orientalism; Algeria; Women

3b50b4cf-8492-533e-8f06-4e7806420158.name: Tsar Nikolai and his family visit Queen Victoria
3b50b4cf-8492-533e-8f06-4e7806420158.short_description: Alix de Hesse-Darmstadt, who became the last Empress of Russia under the name Alexandra Romanova, was the granddaughter of none other than Queen Victoria of England. Nikolai II and his wife Alexandra stopped off in England on the way to Paris for their official trip in 1896, to introduce their first child (Olga) to her great-grandmother, Queen Victoria.  This photo is more of a family portrait than an official image.
keywords: Diplomacy; Russia; England; Nicholas II; Victoria

3c582e3e-a495-54db-b958-c92ae0736f0c.name: Portrait miniature of the Qajar ruler, Fath ‘Ali Shah
3c582e3e-a495-54db-b958-c92ae0736f0c.short_description: This miniature portrait of Fath ‘Ali Shah was signed by Baqir, a versatile enamel painter, who produced high-quality work for the Qajar dynasty. He signed the miniature portrait as ‘the slave born in the household Baqir’, which stressed his role as a craftsman in the royal workshop. In this miniature Fath ‘Ali Shah is portrayed as a relatively young man, with a short beard and continuous eyebrows. He is richly dressed and wears several necklaces, armbands and a tall astrakhan hat decorated with an aigrette, possibly booty from the Mughal treasury in Delhi. To the left of the portrait there is a teardrop-shaped cartouche, which bears the inscription: ‘Fath ‘Ali Shah Qajar’.

3d283460-a96d-52c9-8396-14cc20cc6366.name: A young algerian girl
3d283460-a96d-52c9-8396-14cc20cc6366.short_description: Between the late 19th century and the 1930s, it became fashionable in the West to take photographs of children, either for publication as postcards or with "anthropological" aims. This photograph highlights the striking contrast between the hardships of poverty and the young girl's smile.

4015cd67-07da-50de-ad09-a73de96638ef.name: Abdul Baha Abbas (1844–1921)
4015cd67-07da-50de-ad09-a73de96638ef.short_description: Born in Tehran, Abbas left Iran because of religious persecution. He travelled widely in Egypt, Europe and the United States. In 1913 he settled in Haifa where he founded the religious sect of Baha'i.

40b694ae-445b-54d8-b559-e424f0a605c7.name: *Alexander Karatheodori Pasha (1833–1906)*
40b694ae-445b-54d8-b559-e424f0a605c7.short_description: Portrait of Alexander Karatheodori Pasha. He was born in 1833 in the Greek quarter, Phanar, in Constantinople and served as leading diplomat (Premier Plénipotentiaire) of the Ottoman Empire at the 1878 Congress of Berlin. With the consent of the Ottoman government, Austro-Hungarian troops occupied Bosnia-Herzegovina.
keywords: Alexander Karatheodori Pasha;Congress of Berlin; Bosnia

41d110ef-ea08-56b4-9331-39d56114f999.name: Portrait of Archduke Maximilian
41d110ef-ea08-56b4-9331-39d56114f999.short_description: Portrait of the Archduke Ferdinand Maximilian, who was commander of the Austrian Navy. In 1855 he visited parts of the Ottoman Empire including Smyrna, Palestine and Egypt.
41d110ef-ea08-56b4-9331-39d56114f999.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
keywords: Ferdinand Maximilian; Smyrna, Palestine; Egypt

42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.name: Portrait of a Lady
42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.description: The decoration of the cabinet represented in this painting is clearly influenced by Islamic art in the details of the arches and the motifs in Neo-Mudéjar style. This decoration is related to the different publications about the Alhambra or the drawings by Carderera, in which the designers and artists found new inspiration for their works.
42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.artist: Antonio Maria Esquivel y Suárez de Urbina
42a12e5a-4f49-5af5-9a9c-e5db696bbced.author: Ana Cabrera
keywords: Women; Neo-mudejar style; Applied Arts

42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.name: The excavation of Mount Nemrut
42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.short_description: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.
keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters; archaeological excavations

43466c72-e5b9-5030-8983-576a5a27f879.name: Alexander I Obrenovic, King of Serbia (1876–1903)
43466c72-e5b9-5030-8983-576a5a27f879.short_description: Portrait of Alexander I Obrenovic, King of Serbia (1876–1903) as a young man. Between the abdication of his father in 1889 and his proclamation as a king in 1893, his mother Natalija Obrenovic ruled as a regent. Being a close ally of Austria, he became Serbian King in 1893. In 1894 Alexander abolished the liberal constitution of Serbia. In 1900 he married Draga Masin, a former lady-in-waiting of his mother. This marriage was very unpopular and weakened the political position of the king. In 1903 he and his wife were murdered by a group of Serbian officers.
keywords: Edmund Count Szecheny; Budapest; Hungary; Istanbul, Ottoman empire; fire brigade

43b2594e-92cf-584f-b624-afc4b94a968d.name: Giovanni Miani (1810–1872)
43b2594e-92cf-584f-b624-afc4b94a968d.short_description: Portrait of Giovanni Miani (1810–1872). Born in Northern Italy, he was an intellectual who was forced by Austrian authorities to seek exile in the Ottoman Empire. He lived in Athens, Smyrna and Egypt and was one of the European explorers who tried to find the sources of the Nile.
keywords: Giovanni Miani; Italy; Egypt; Nile

453156d3-f141-581a-96a5-4ef8c83cbae1.name: Dr Charles Nicolle
453156d3-f141-581a-96a5-4ef8c83cbae1.short_description: Pictured here is Dr. Charles Nicolle, a French microbiology doctor born in Rouen on 21 September 1966, in his research laboratory. His name is strongly linked to l'Institut Pasteur, which he directed from 1903–1936, playing the role of administrator, researcher, school headmaster, and advocate for the teaching of hygiene and illness prevention. In 1928 he received the Nobel Prize for Physiology. He died in 1936 and is buried at the Institut Pasteur, where his tombstone is engraved with olive and apple tree branches crossed over, the symbols of Tunisia and Normandy.
453156d3-f141-581a-96a5-4ef8c83cbae1.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
keywords: Doctors of Tunisia; hospital; vaccination

4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.name: Mohamed Daghabi
4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.short_description: Born in El Hamma to the Beni Zid tribe (near Gabès), Mohamed Daghbagi (1885–1924) became a deserter in 1915, after the battle of Dhibat between the French troops and the Tunisian resistance. In 1920 he rose to fame through his role in an armed group which took part in various conflicts. He then took refuge in Tripolitaine, and was arrested in 1922 and given back to the French. He was executed in El Hamma on 1 March 1924.
4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.author: Bechir Yazidi
keywords: French protectorate; resistance; occupation

459c2899-4ce2-5ffd-a17b-a43ffa91c9bc.name: *Milos Obrenovic, prince of Serbia*
459c2899-4ce2-5ffd-a17b-a43ffa91c9bc.short_description: Milos Obrenović (1783-1860) was Prince of Serbia from 1815 to 1839, and again from 1858 to 1860. He participated in the First Serbian Uprising, led Serbs in the Second Serbian Uprising, and founded the dynasty of Obrenović. Under his rule, Serbia became an autonomous duchy within the Ottoman Empire. He is credited with starting the process of re-establishing Serbian statehood, as well as shaping the domestic and foreign policies of the modern Serbian state. Prince Milos ruled autocratically, permanently refusing to share power. During his rule, he was the richest man in Serbia and among the richest in the Balkans. In the portrait that was painted by Pavel Djurkovitch in Kragujevac, prince Milos is dressed in Oriental costume and has on the top of the head a turban. It is a typically Oriental piece of costume and this was of significance for the attitude and dignity of the Serbian sovereign at the beginning 19th century, who was by all means respecting an Ottoman empire and his Sultan.
459c2899-4ce2-5ffd-a17b-a43ffa91c9bc.author: Petar Petrovic
keywords: Self representation; Orientalism

47de166a-64f2-5809-807d-457eb735b800.name: Stefan Petrovic Knicanin (1809–1855)
47de166a-64f2-5809-807d-457eb735b800.short_description: Portrait of Stefan Petrovic Knicanin. The Serbian officer Stefan Petrovic Knicanin supported the Austrian Emperor during the 1848 revolution. In 1849 he returned to Serbia and fostered good relations between Serbia and Austria. He died in 1855 in Belgrade.
keywords: Stefan Petrovic Knicanin; Serbia

48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century

49a80737-c924-5479-8273-7392e3cd1db8.name: Gjorgij Pulevski
49a80737-c924-5479-8273-7392e3cd1db8.short_description: Gjorgji Pulevski was a prominent figure of the Macedonian Enlightenment. He was born in Galichnik in 1822 and died in Sofia in 1893. In 1873, during his stay in Belgrade, he published the ”Dictionary of Four Languages,” which included Macedonian, Albanian, Greek and Turkish words. His “Dictionary of Three Languages” was issued in 1875. Gjorgji Pulevski was the founder of the Macedonian Literary Society, established in Sofia in 1888. It was one of the independent associations of Macedonian emigrants that made contributions to the awakening of the Macedonian national spirit.
49a80737-c924-5479-8273-7392e3cd1db8.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
keywords: Enlightenment

49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.name: Turkman Prisoner
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.short_description: The Turkoman prisoner is a common subject in Iranian art. The motif was copied and subtly interpreted in both drawings and paintings, which were probably intended for placement in albums. The prisoner depicted here, as in all such representations, is fettered by a *palahang*, a device made from a forked branch, to which one wrist is attached by an additional band of wood or metal. A crossbar at the back of the prisoner’s neck completes the restraint. As is typical, the prisoners’ physiognomy and clothes denote his Turkman ethnicity. He wears a sleeveless outer robe over a long-sleeved tunic, with an elaborately knotted sash; his head is covered by a peaked cap. Characteristically, he carries a sheathed sword, a dagger, a quiver with arrows, a bow and case, a flail, and a whip. Not surprising, given his extensive armaments, he does not seem humbled by his captivity; rather, apart from the introduction of the shackling yoke, such prisoner figures are often nearly indistinguishable from contemporaneous paintings of similarly clothed and armed Uzbek princes or warriors. Based on the Persian poetry by Amir Shahi of Sabzavar (d. 857/1453), which surrounds the painting, it is possible to suggest a less literal meaning for this prisoner imagery. The verses give voice to the torments of unrequited love, a common theme in classical Persian poetry. Claiming to haunt the street of the beloved by night, the lover moans, "Happy is that prisoner who has someone to come to his rescue," which is inscribed, almost like a caption beneath the bent leg of the captive.
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.dates: Hegira second half of 10th century / AD second half of 16th century
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.method_for_datation: The motif of the Turkman prisoner first appears in Persian painting around the middle of the sixteenth century. The LACMA painting is very similar to one in a Persian-made album in the Topkapi Palace Library, Istanbul, H. 2156, which has margins dated between Hegira 980 / AD 1572 and Hegira 982 /AD 1575. This strong similarity suggests that a tracing was made from the Topkapi version, perhaps datable to the 1560s to early 1570s, which was reversed and used as pounce to produce the LACMA painting.
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.method_for_provenance: The motif of the Turkman prisoner is known primarily in Safavid painting; a few instances occur in Mughal India.
49ea5362-039b-5261-908a-c40c047fa0bb.obtention: Collection of Roland Yazhari, Portland, Oregon, until 2000 (sold to); LACMA, gift of the Ancient Art Council, Iran Trip 2000.

4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.name: Antonio del Valle y Serrano, Marquis of Villa-Huerta
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait shows the elegance and the character of Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marquis of Villa-Huerta and stepson of the marquis of Cerralbo.
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
keywords: Portrait; souvenir; memorabilia

4dcb750e-6c2b-5848-924b-43fb6905059d.name: Memorial Volume – Dedicatory and opening ceremonies of the Chicago World's Colombian Exposition – 1893
4dcb750e-6c2b-5848-924b-43fb6905059d.short_description: The World's Columbian Exposition or The Chicago World's Fair was a World's Fair held in Chicago in 1893 to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World in 1492. The fair was an influential social and cultural event to which the Ottoman Empire had been invited. It displayed raw materials and agricultural products at the exposition, as well as handicraft products and plant products belonging to the palace revenue. The 1893 Chicago Exhibition was a big success for the Chamber of Commerce. The Head of the Chamber of Commerce, Azaryan Efendi, was assigned to the head of the commission, which was formed in Istanbul for the Chicago Exhibition.
keywords: International Exhibitions; exposition; fair

4ed1534b-d859-5994-b88b-5db059e74f6c.name: *Ferdinand III as King of Hungary*
4ed1534b-d859-5994-b88b-5db059e74f6c.description: The history of the painting is connected to the Diet of Sopron in 1625. In November 1625, the 18 year-old Habsburg heir was crowned King of Hungary in Sopron as Ferdinand III. Participating envoys reported that for the occasion the interior decoration of the Franciscan Church of Sopron consisted of the heraldic red, white and green of Hungary. The prospective ruler was also dressed for the ceremony in this vein: in the attire of a Hungarian nobleman, as seen in this portrait. The young king's first official portrait, the painting is an important document of the coronation, its authenticity seen in the faithful depiction of the Hungarian Holy Crown, rarely seen at the time. Such a detailed depiction, correct even in the colours used, would have been possible only by observation. As an object deprived of “publicity”, the crown was on display during coronation ceremonies only. This means that the artist must have attended the crowning ceremony. The portrait is attributed to the Flemish painter Justus Sustermans – court painter of the Medici in Florence – by analogy of his contemporaneous works, and by the fact that he had visited the Habsburg court on an earlier occasion and worked on commissions for the imperial family. There is probably more than one version of *Ferdinand III as King of Hungary*, this one becoming part of the collection of a notable Spanish art collector, connoisseur and collector of portraits, Marquis Leganés, Don Diego Da Messia. Leganés was busy at the time arranging the marriage of Ferdinand III and the Infanta, Maria Anna, sister of Philip III King of Spain, which was schedule for the spring of 1626.
4ed1534b-d859-5994-b88b-5db059e74f6c.short_description: The history of the painting is connected to the Diet of Sopron in 1625. Participating envoys reported that for the occasion the interior decoration of the Franciscan Church of Sopron consisted of the heraldic red, white and green of Hungary. In this commemorative painting, the first official portrait of the 18 year-old Ferdinand III as King of Hungary, he is dressed in these colours. An important detail of the painting is the accurate depiction of the Hungarian Holy Crown, seen in every detail and accurately depicted enriched by the same colours.
4ed1534b-d859-5994-b88b-5db059e74f6c.method_for_datation: By historical data and stylistic analysis

4efddfdd-e8a3-5895-9f9c-d7247e51a06f.name: Portrait of an unknown scholar
4efddfdd-e8a3-5895-9f9c-d7247e51a06f.short_description:
This portrait depicts a calligrapher or scholar, wearing a white turban and with a red beard dyed with henna. Crouched in the corner of a simple room, lost in thought, he holds the mouthpiece of his water pipe. To his left, on top of a chest, a few personal objects include a pair of spectacles, a silver pocket watch, pencil cases, a book and a small glass vase with a bunch-flowered narcissus (*Narcissus tazetta*).  
  
We know almost nothing about the painter, Mirza Aqa, mentioned in the poem accompanying this portrait. The qualities of this work are due in particular to the pictorial technique used by the painter. The faithful, almost rough rendering of the face gives the figure a strong, penetrating presence. The play of perspective, light and shadow, and the realism shown by the painter can be found in other contemporary Qajar painters.
4efddfdd-e8a3-5895-9f9c-d7247e51a06f.method_for_datation: By comparison with similar dated works.
4efddfdd-e8a3-5895-9f9c-d7247e51a06f.method_for_provenance: By comparison with stylistically similar works.
4efddfdd-e8a3-5895-9f9c-d7247e51a06f.bibliography: Langer, Axel, “Portrait d’un érudit, ” in Gwenaëlle Fellinger (ed), *L’Empire des roses. Chefs-d’oeuvres de l’art persan du XIXe siècle*, exh. cat., Ghent and Lens: Éditions Snoeck and Louvre Lens, 2018: 244-245.
4efddfdd-e8a3-5895-9f9c-d7247e51a06f.author: Axel Langer

5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.name: El Sayyid Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889–1983), from 1916 Chief of the Senussi Muslim order
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.short_description: El Sayyid (or Sidi) Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889-1983), the grandson of the founder of the Senussi Sufi order, became head of the Senussi order in 1916. He took the title of Emir and ruled as King of Libya from 1951 through 1969. In 1920 Italy reached an agreement with him and invited him to Rome, where he met King Victor Emmanuel III. Idris’ relations with the Italian government later deteriorated, and he went into exile in Egypt and encouraged anti-Italian guerrilla from there.
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.author: Giulia Barrera

50b3f8f9-ce03-5830-9814-d4eedeb46a2e.name: *Ivan III Adam Ratkay*
50b3f8f9-ce03-5830-9814-d4eedeb46a2e.description:
The Ratkays were a noble family originating from Hungary whose family name is spelled in several different ways: Rathkay, Rattkay, Ratkay. In 1502, the Ratkays gained possession of the castle and estate of Veliki Tabor in north-west Croatia. From thereon they called themselves “Ratkay de Nagy Tabor”. Marriage connects the Ratkays to the Croatian nobility.  
Ivan III (Veliki Tabor, Croatia, 1640–Mexico, 1683) was a page at the court of Emperor Leopold I. He studied philosophy and theology in Graz before becoming a Jesuit, and was ordained in 1676. In 1678, he departed via Genoa, Seville and Cadiz for Mexico, landing in Vera Cruz two years later. From 1681, he lived among the Tarahumara Indians as a missionary, dying there from the effects of a native poison in 1683. He wrote journals of his travels in Latin, documenting his journey to Mexico and New Mexico, which he enriched with a map of Tarahumara with missionary settlements and Spanish fortresses (thereby making him one of the first Croatian cartographers). The family died out at the end of the 18th century.  
The painting consists of a portrait, four scenes from his life as a Jesuit, and a family coat of arms, all in separate painted frames. This painting is unique in the Museum collection in that it depicts the short life of the missionary in a series of smaller scenes arranged around the central oval with the portrait of Ivan III. It was painted by an unknown artist in the first decades of the 18th century.
50b3f8f9-ce03-5830-9814-d4eedeb46a2e.short_description: From a noble family, Ivan III had been a page at the court of Emperor Leopold I. He studied philosophy and read law before becoming a Jesuit. In 1678, he departed for America landing in Vera Cruz two years later. Working as a missionary among the American Indians, he died there from the effects of a native poison in 1683. He wrote journals of his travels in Latin and drew a map of the territory where he worked, making him one of the first Croatian cartographers.
50b3f8f9-ce03-5830-9814-d4eedeb46a2e.method_for_datation: The date and origin of the painting were established by the inscription and from study of the information about the person depicted.
50b3f8f9-ce03-5830-9814-d4eedeb46a2e.obtention: Unknown; in the Museum collection since before 1920.

5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.name: Portrait of Paul Draneht
5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.short_description:
Paul Draneht (1815-1894) was born in Nicosia (Cyprus) as Pavlos Pavlidis. He was the child of a Greek Christian Orthodox family who fled Cyprus due to the clashes between Greeks and Turks, and took refuge in Egypt. Muhammad (Mehmet) Ali Pasha (the Khedive of Egypt) sent him to study in France. Trusted by the Khedive (who awarded him the titles of Bey and Pasha), Paul Draneht participated in the negotiations regarding the opening of the Suez Canal.  
He became superintendent of the Egyptian Opera Theatre and commissioned the opera Aida to the Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi. The Aida opened in Cairo on 24 December 1871.
5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella

532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.name: *A young and an old Turk*
532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.short_description: Carol Popp de Szathmari was born in Transylvania, but later settled in Bucharest, Wallachia, where he worked as court painter of princes Alexandru Dimitrie Ghica, Gheorghe Bibescu and Alexandru Ioan Cuza. During the reign of prince Carol of Hohenzollern, he was also court photographer. He is the author of five photographic albums with images of people and places from Bucharest and other regions in Romania, among which there are depictions of people belonging to the ethnic minorities of Romania, such as the Turks. He travelled twice to Istanbul, in 1860 and 1864, as member of prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza’s suite. During the Crimean War (1854-1855) he photographed the Russian and Turkish armies that occupied Wallachia and then went to Crimea, where he took more than 200 photos of the fights.

54f5684d-16ac-5378-a06c-a89a79ec2891.name: *Portrait of Marcello Sacchetti*
54f5684d-16ac-5378-a06c-a89a79ec2891.description:
Pietro Berrettini, also known as Cortona, was one of the key figures in Roman Baroque art, both as a painter and an architect.  
The subject of this portrait, Marcello Sacchetti, was made depositary general and secret treasurer of the Apostolic Chamber in 1623 thanks to his relationship with Maffeo Barberini, who had just become Pope Urban VIII. The artist painted this portrait after 1623 but before 1629, the year that Sacchetti died. A date around 1626 is generally accepted.  
The relationship between painter and patron was important, not just because Berrettini was given some major commissions by the Sacchetti family between 1627 and 1629, but for its exemplary nature.  
Well integrated in Roman social and cultural circles, the nobleman Sacchetti introduced Berrettini to the most important collectors, allowing him to obtain new and interesting commissions and to consolidate his relationship with the powerful Barberinis.  
Sacchetti, a banker and businessman, is painted by the artist in a pose that successfully transmits the refinement of the gentleman, dressed in dark colours with collar and cuffs in fine white lace, with a pleasing spontaneity. Leaning casually against a fine console of richly decorated gilded wood, with the family coat of arms at the centre, through his deep gaze, he emits with proud nobility a psychological strength filled with feeling.  
The style is enhanced by an atmosphere rendered through the use of light and dark built up with intense brushstrokes, effortlessly achieving a perfection of form, reinforced by the chosen pose, a dazzling silk handkerchief in his hand.  
The painting may be one of a cycle of seven “Standing portraits of the Sacchetti” mentioned in a 1639 inventory. In 1644, the canvas is mentioned in an inventory by Antonio Barberini. It is not known how it became part of the Borghese collection, where it was documented in 1833 and where it was enlarged to serve as a pendant to the *Portrait of Monsignor Clemente Merlini* by Andrea Sacchi. The painting was restored and returned to its original dimensions in 1931.
54f5684d-16ac-5378-a06c-a89a79ec2891.short_description: Pietro da Cortona was commissioned by Sacchetti, one of the most important collectors in Rome, on numerous occasions for his family homes. The nobleman is shown in a spontaneous pose beside a valuable table, showing his refined taste.
54f5684d-16ac-5378-a06c-a89a79ec2891.obtention: The Borghese Collection was acquired by the Italian State in 1902.

562cd119-0bf1-544d-a90a-b4094899b356.name: Arabi, Sayed Ahmed Pasha (1841–1911)
562cd119-0bf1-544d-a90a-b4094899b356.short_description: Portrait of minister Sayed Ahmed Pasha Arabi (Urabi). In 1882, the war minister took power in Egypt and demanded an end to the financial control imposed by the UK and France. This led to an intervention by the British Navy under Admiral Seymour, who defeated the Egyptian army.
