5686a4e1-e33b-5ad7-8f7a-20b3b101f2ca.name: Petar (Pezia) Petrovich (2nd half of the 19th century – 1900)
5686a4e1-e33b-5ad7-8f7a-20b3b101f2ca.short_description: Portrait of Petar (Pezia) Petrovic. He was Chief of the Albanian Mirdita tribes fighting against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.

568aa288-3d05-5bf2-9461-11f5d3c78666.name: *Portrait of Charles of Bourbon*
568aa288-3d05-5bf2-9461-11f5d3c78666.description:
The Portrait of Charles of Bourbon (Charles III of Spain), one of a pair together with a portrait depicting Queen Maria Amalia of Saxony, now lost, is one of the first creations of the Royal Tapestry Factory in Naples.  
Founded by the young King in 1737, soon after his arrival in Naples, the tapestry factory, together with a factory for the carving of semiprecious stones, was one of the first established by order of Charles of Bourbon. This decision must have been influenced by the young Charles’ interest in the Medici factories that were still operating in Florence. This interest developed when the future King stayed in the city in 1732, as the future successor to Gian Gastone de’ Medici.  
In fact, a small group of Florentine weavers and carvers of precious stones was responsible for giving life to the first two royal Bourbon factories in Naples, located near the church of San Carlo alle Mortelle. The factory, which was also composed of a local workforce, with the aim of promoting the development of new artistic techniques in the Kingdom of Naples, was under the direction of the Florentine Domenico del Rosso. And it was to the Florentine weaver that Charles entrusted his portrait and that of his consort; as with other items produced during the initial phase of the factories, these works were intended to celebrate the King and their patron. Production of the tapestry was completed in 1741, as indicated by the presence of the signature and date on the bottom right-hand edge of the tapestry: “DOM.CO D. L. ROSSO 1741”. The artist who provided the preparatory study for the tapestry is unknown; however, there is speculation that it may have been Giovan Battista delle Piane, who was a court portrait painter during these years; or Francesco Solimena, based on the tapestry’s extraordinary expressiveness and the intensity of the light and the colours in its original state.
568aa288-3d05-5bf2-9461-11f5d3c78666.method_for_datation: Signed and dated: “DOM.CO D. L. ROSSO 1741”

582a237b-27f7-5d01-9b51-c2c6abbdd759.name: Metal plate from India
582a237b-27f7-5d01-9b51-c2c6abbdd759.short_description: The object is a metal plate from India portraying Jahangir Shah, the fourth Mughal emperor of India, and his wife, Nur Jahan. Against a black metal background, Jahangir wears traditional Mughal courtier clothes decorated with gold bands and is armed with a long sword at his waist. He holds his last and most favourite wife, whom he married in 1611.  He gazes at her, and the expression of his face in profile, along with his hand on her arm, clearly represents his admiration for the Empress. The empress is armed with a dagger on her hip, decorated with a golden head of a lion. She holds a fan in her right hand, engraved with her title in gold. In her left hand, she holds a pipe, connected to the hookah on the other side of Jahangir. At the top, the metal plate is engraved with the Persian words, "Lady Nur Jahan and the Emperor Jahangir." It is remarkable that Nur Jahan is mentioned prior to the Emperor.
keywords: Mughal; Nur Jahan; Jahangir

5838d2ce-d94c-553a-ba3e-9f697d70d8a3.short_description: Some members of F.J. Bliss’ workforce at Tell el-Hesi. What is most noteworthy here is that in the period up to 1938 men, women, and children all worked together on excavations.

59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.name: Bakırköy Railway Station
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.short_description: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

59e91077-81f0-5cb2-9fc1-2e7eb98c95ab.name: Turkish woman
59e91077-81f0-5cb2-9fc1-2e7eb98c95ab.short_description: The Zangaki brothers were a pair of photographers working in Egypt who sold "Orientalist" photos to Western tourists. This photograph for example, responds to Western stereotypes by depicting a Turkish woman lying nonchalantly by shisha pipe.

5be7c4c7-6d3d-5df5-96ec-e6d5e56acbcd.name: *Portrait of Johann Lenner, City Judge of Pest*
5be7c4c7-6d3d-5df5-96ec-e6d5e56acbcd.description:
The carpenter, Johann Lenner, left Germany for Pest where his craftsmanship was required in the rebuilding of the city following the end of Ottoman rule. Lenner obtained nobility through his craftsmanship and became a city judge. After four years as city judge, he served in Pest as a councillor for the 10 years that followed. As a result of Lenner's work the city amassed a large sum of money with which it supported the foundation of a Piarist school in Pest in 1717. An inscription on the back of this painting reads *“Johann Lenner de Lennersberg primarius Juder Liberae Regiaque Civitatis Pesthiensis quo potissimum agente Scholae Piae Anno 1717”*.  
The half-length portrait represents Lenner standing. He is dressed in a dignified manner, wearing a wig and a cloak. This painting is one of the earliest examples in a series of official portraits of chief officials of the city of Pest.
5be7c4c7-6d3d-5df5-96ec-e6d5e56acbcd.short_description: An early example of a representational portrait of a city official.

5d7ce667-91be-5456-a2b0-7cd880b231f3.name: *Portrait of Ruđer Bošković*
5d7ce667-91be-5456-a2b0-7cd880b231f3.description:
In this portrait world-famed Croatian scientist Ruđer Bošković (1711–1787) is 45 years of age as stated in the legend under the painting. Seen in his study, with his published works arranged on a shelf, he sits in an armchair, at his desk, dressed in the Jesuit uniform of black cassock and a cap. In his right hand, he holds compasses while his left hand rests on a planetarium; his face looks out to the observer. The colours have an overall brown tone and the portrait is faithful, though of only mediocre quality. Painted by an unknown Italian painter, Bošković was teaching mathematics in Rome at the time.  
Beneath the portrait is an inscription in Latin:  
P.ROGERIUVS BOSCOVICH S.I.IN COLLEGIO ROM.MAT. PROFES.  
NATUS RAGUSIJ XV KAL. IVNIJ MDCCXI AETATIS ANNO XLV  
Bošković was a leading physicist, mathematician, astronomer, philosopher and writer. Born in Dubrovnik, he was educated at the Jesuit college there and then in Rome. In 1725, he entered the Society of Jesus and remained in it until its dissolution in 1773. He was a professor at many schools and universities throughout Italy and travelled throughout Europe. A member of many academies, he published numerous scientific works. He was an all-round intellectual that studied and taught archaeology, literature, philosophy and rhetoric, and, in addition, worked as a diplomat. At the end of his life, his mental health suffered, and he died completely exhausted from pneumonia in 1773.
5d7ce667-91be-5456-a2b0-7cd880b231f3.short_description:
A portrait of the world-famed Croatian scientist, Ruđer Bošković (1711–1787), painted in the mid-18th century by an unknown artist. The portrait shows him sitting in his study surrounded by the many books he wrote and clad in the habit of the Jesuits. In his right hand, he holds compasses while his left hand rests on a planetarium. According to the legend at the bottom of the painting, the portrait dates to 1756 when Bošković was teaching mathematics in Rome aged 45.  
This leading physicist, mathematician, astronomer, philosopher and writer, born in Dubrovnik, educated at the Jesuit college there and then in Rome, entered the Society of Jesus in 1725 and remained in it until its dissolution in 1773.
5d7ce667-91be-5456-a2b0-7cd880b231f3.holder: Museum of Icons of the Serbian Orthodox Church Community
5d7ce667-91be-5456-a2b0-7cd880b231f3.method_for_datation: According to a legend at the bottom of the painting, the painting portrays Bošković at the age of 45. Therefore, since he was born in 1711, the portrait dates to 1756.
5d7ce667-91be-5456-a2b0-7cd880b231f3.obtention: Donated by the Serbian Orthodox Church Community in Dubrovnik.

5e9e845e-5f4e-508c-91ed-f52d967dbf97.short_description: Black and white photo in a family album: A family gathering at the garden of Emmanuel Benaki’s mansion in Alexandria. 5fafc343-ccfd-52d3-8bd4-f2f311ffa1cf.name: *Bust of Clement XII*
5fafc343-ccfd-52d3-8bd4-f2f311ffa1cf.description:
Pietro Bracci produced a large number of works, mainly portraits. He was one of the most important late Baroque sculptors of the 18th century in Rome, and was involved in the creation of the Trevi Fountain. He was trained in the Baroque tradition based on the work of Gian Lorenzo Bernini and classical equilibrium.  
There is no documentary evidence linking the bust to the sculptor, nor any explicit references in the work-log that Bracci was in the habit of keeping after 1725, but the attribution is generally accepted by scholars.  
It is dated around the time of the pontificate of Clement XII Corsini, which lasted from 1730 to 1740, although it is possible that the bust was made after his death.  
The ageing face of the pope is sculpted faithfully, reproducing the lines infused with deep expressiveness and intelligence, key characteristics of the artist's portraits. The pontificate's vestments are finely decorated and tied at the chest, while the fur-trimmed cloak and underlying *mozzetta*  
(a short elbow length cape worn by Catholic clergy) are sculpted to achieve an elegant volume of folds that create a play of light and shadow.  
There are other busts of the pope, although full information is not available for all of them. Of particular interest is the one currently in Ravenna, which may have been intended for the pontificate's tomb in Laterano, and the bust of Clement XII, currently exhibited in the Galleria Nazionale di Arte Antica, which was acquired in 1927.  
The portrait of the pope in the Galleria Borghese was donated to the museum in 1910 by the Istituto dei Ciechi at the Baths of Diocletian.
5fafc343-ccfd-52d3-8bd4-f2f311ffa1cf.short_description: Pietro Bracci follows the Baroque tradition seen in Bernini's psychological portrait, *Cardinal Scipione Borghese*. Bracci was one of the sculptors involved in the creation of the Trevi Fountain.

60d2a3da-9b0d-5e19-af72-c7ddc1d18f65.name: Portrait of an officer Dusan T. Urošević
60d2a3da-9b0d-5e19-af72-c7ddc1d18f65.description: Portrait of Dušan T. Urošević, an officer, shows a Pirot kilim as a prop on the floor of the photographer’s studio in Niš. The border of the kilim is decorated with *Queen’s sleeve* (*kraljičin rukav*) ornament. As it was common in late 19th and early 20th century, the subject wasn’t portrayed in a real-life environment, but in carefully staged photographer’s studio setting. Besides the Pirot kilim and furniture, other props used in the studio were a curtain, a tablecloth, a vase with the flowers and a book.

6215ebc8-8b3b-5484-8ac2-a702cc00efad.name: Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) / Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
6215ebc8-8b3b-5484-8ac2-a702cc00efad.short_description: Portrait of Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) on horseback/ Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen. He was elected Prince of Romania on the recommendation of Napoleon III in 1866. In 1881, after achieving formal independence from the Ottoman Empire, Carol declared himself King of Romania.

629911e6-06d2-536a-9acd-824991f44ffa.name: Ferdinand, King of Romania (1865–1927) / Ferdinand von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
629911e6-06d2-536a-9acd-824991f44ffa.short_description: Portrait of Ferdinand I, King of Romania. After the death of King Carol I, Ferdinand (as the nephew of the deceased king) ascended to the throne. In 1916 he joined the *entente* and declared war against Austria and Germany. After World War I, Romania gained Transylvania, Bukowina and the Banat from Austria, and Bessarabia from Russia. Ferdinand died in Romania in 1927.
keywords: Romania; Ferdinand I

647bb6c0-14ae-506b-85c5-060226c34178.name: Poet Nigar Hanım
647bb6c0-14ae-506b-85c5-060226c34178.short_description: Nigar Hanım, who was born in Istanbul in 1856, studied in a French school. She also took private Turkish, Arabic and Persian classes. She started to write poems when she was a child. She had a very good command of the French language and French literature. Every Tuesday, she gathered reputable personalities at her place, where they discussed art and literature, listened to music and read poems. She collected her poems in *Efsûs I* (1877), *Efsûs II* (1891), *Nîram* (1896), *Aks-i Seda* (1900) and *Elhan-i Vatan* (1916). She also wrote a work of prose in 1901 entitled *Safahat-i Kalb*. A fine lyricism that expresses her unhappiness in her private life can be observed in her work. Among the Turkish poets, she was the most productive, writing very original pieces in the second half of the 19th century.

65011066-4ed5-5528-a635-0088b486989b.name: Portrait of Cardinal Sembratowicz
65011066-4ed5-5528-a635-0088b486989b.description:
Sylwester Sembratowicz (1836–98) had been metropolitan Archbishop of Lviv (in Polish Lwów or Lvov), of the Greek-Catholic denomination, since 1885. In 1895, he became Cardinal. He was also a professor and Dean of the Theological Faculty at the Jan Kazimierz University in Lviv.  
Cardinal Sembratowicz is depicted sitting on a highly decorated armchair in the sacral interior, behind him is a lectern covered with embroidered drapery. Beneath his feet, we see a precious carpet, probably a Persian carpet of the Tabriz type. On the carpet’s softly painted surface it is possible to recognise an ornament of elaborately woven palmettes, with many colourful details that are joined with wavy tendrils, on a red ground. The border is dark-blue, filled with a row of palmettes. Persian carpets were very popular among wealthy inhabitants of Lviv in the 19th and 20th centuries. A very similar carpet, dating to the 19th century, is preserved in the collections of the National Museum in Kraków (inv. no. MNK XIX-12064). In spite of this carpet’s generous dimensions, the Janelli family took it with them into exile when forced to leave Lviv by the Soviet authorities in 1946.

Zięba, Andrzej A., “Sylwester Sembratowicz”, *Polski Słownik Biograficzny* (Polish Biographical Dictionary), vol. XXXVI/2, fasc. 145, Warsaw and Kraków: Polish Academy of Sciences, 1995: 212‒16.

65f0147e-2ea5-57c6-89c2-25c7b8e3c09c.name: *Count Paar as Neptune*
65f0147e-2ea5-57c6-89c2-25c7b8e3c09c.description:
Count Josef Ignaz Paar, High Steward of Emperor Joseph I and curator of the Vienna-Academy, and his wife, Marie Anna of Valdštejn, the empress's lady-in-waiting, initiated the transformation of the Renaissance chateau in Budišov into a spectacular mansion in 1715. Only a few of the rooms with their Baroque interiors have survived: the *sala terrena* with chinoiseries and the Ancient (Golden) Room on the second floor, decorated with grotesque paintings and featuring scenes from the lives of ancient gods that also personify the elements. Crypto-portraits in the room beside it crown the elaborate decoration of the chateau, a typical example of the residences of court nobility at the time. The ground floor features hunting scenes with the god, Zeus, conveying the fate of the interconnection between earthly pleasures and tribulations. The paintings on the first floor depict the course of the world through the changing seasons, while on the second floor there are pictures from the lives of the high gods. The second large painting shows the countess Paar as *Amfitríté*. The Triptychon illustrate the Devise “*Omnia vincit amor*” – that love wins over all – and originally they decorated the wedding room, now known as “the room of elements”.  
Only a fragment of Prenner's, the court painter of Maria Theresa, work has survived. Walter Xaver of Dietrichstein commissioned him with the restoration of the Mikulov chateau; Prenner was also his artistic advisor. The artist worked for Jan Adam Questenberk (Rapoltenkirchen, Jaroměřice nad Rokytnou). As director of the Vienna court art collections, he captured their treasures in a series of engravings, *Theatrum artis poctoriae* and *Prodromus*.
65f0147e-2ea5-57c6-89c2-25c7b8e3c09c.short_description: Crypto-portraits of the counts in the room crown the elaborate decoration of the chateau, an example typical of the residences of court nobility at the time. Count Paar was a High Steward of Emperor Joseph I and curator of the Vienna-Academy. Only a fragment of Prenner’s work, the count painter, has survived.

65fd829c-bfae-5827-bf9b-ed418624bfa6.name: Ferdinand I, King of Romania (1865–1927) / Ferdinand von Hohenzollen-Sigmaringen
65fd829c-bfae-5827-bf9b-ed418624bfa6.short_description: Street Scene with King Ferdinand of Romania in Vienna. After the death of King Carol I, Ferdinand (as the nephew of the deceased king) ascended to the throne. In 1916 he joined the *entente* and declared war against Austria and Germany. After World War I, Romania gained Transylvania, Bukowina and the Banat from Austria, and Bessarabia from Russia. Ferdinand died in Romania in 1927.
keywords: Ferdinand I, King of Romania

67e4f746-f9b3-5718-ba2d-1a3899a55af1.name: Water Glass
67e4f746-f9b3-5718-ba2d-1a3899a55af1.description:
The tall glass is cylindrical in shape and rests on a low circular stem and base. It is decorated with an oval medallion on the front featuring a photographic portrait of King Alexander and Queen Draga Obrenović against a white background. The oval medallion is highlighted with a partially gilded ornament of stylized leaves and vine strips. Two thin gilded lines encircle the rim.  
This type of glass featuring a royal portrait had been appearing in Serbia since the mid-19th century. Portraits of the Obrenović dynasty were often applied to glass tableware. It is presumed that they were most likely produced as memorabilia. The glass with King Alexander and Queen Draga's portrait can certainly be interpreted in terms of promoting the last royal couple of the House of Obrenović.
67e4f746-f9b3-5718-ba2d-1a3899a55af1.method_for_datation: By stylistic analysis and comparative method using other objects made in the same period in the same place.
67e4f746-f9b3-5718-ba2d-1a3899a55af1.bibliography: Djurić, J., *Staklo, u Srbiji XIX veka* (Glass in 19th Century Serbia), exhibition catalogue, Belgrade: Muzej primenjene umetnosti (Museum of Applied Art), 1985: 83.

materials: Colourless, blown glass with applied photo decoration

6857e440-8f5f-5412-a588-b0da5f2afb45.name: *Bust of the Cardinal Scipione Borghese*
6857e440-8f5f-5412-a588-b0da5f2afb45.description:
In 1605 when Paul V became Pope, he immediately made his nephew Scipione a cardinal, despite his young age, quickly promoting him to a position comparable to secretary of state. This enormous power allowed the cardinal-nephew to create a splendid home and a marvellous art collection over a decade, in an unorthodox manner.  
The bust portrait of Scipione by Gian Lorenzo Bernini was sculpted for his first major patron in 1632, after a creative hiatus of nearly seven years as a sculptor, during which he developed a new concept in portraits, more representative of the vibrant Baroque style.  
The spontaneous and intense pose, the arrangement of the bust with the head turned in a slight movement, the attentive gaze and the mouth open in an expression of vague wonderment combine to create a highly expressive, almost colloquial relation with the viewer.  
The cloth folds in the *mozzetta* (a short elbow length cape worn by Catholic clergy) and the detail of the small unfastened button showing us the live body beneath the clothes are an integral and involving part of the piece.  
The marked confidence displayed by this excellent example of a Baroque style of which Bernini was a master gives an intimate and human dimension to the sitter, despite his official status.  
With the bust almost finished, a hairline fracture opened up in the marble around the forehead, due to the stresses of the sculpting tools. The sculptor was forced to produce a second version of the bust at very short notice. This shows how little attention Bernini paid to his choice of marble, something that was of fundamental importance for other sculptors, such as Michelangelo. Despite the crack, the Cardinal requested that both works be delivered to him, keeping both in the Galleria Borghese.
6857e440-8f5f-5412-a588-b0da5f2afb45.short_description: Cardinal Borghese, the pope’s nephew, was a passionate collector and looked after the cultural policy of the papal court. He had a sensitive instinct for artistic quality and gave a boost to the birth of the Baroque. Bernini renders the Cardinal life-like; the transience of human feeling and the expression of inner emotions are part of the Baroque aesthetic.
6857e440-8f5f-5412-a588-b0da5f2afb45.obtention: The Borghese Collection was acquired by the Italian State in 1902.

68850fe9-86ff-5692-8ae9-7d758c18ca87.name: *Letta Asım Baloya Giderken* (*Letta Asım was about to go to a ball*)
68850fe9-86ff-5692-8ae9-7d758c18ca87.short_description: As a result of modernization efforts and the increase in relations with the West in the 19th century, there were significant changes in Ottoman social life. Instead of the traditional 18th-century entertainment which consisted of miniatures, in Tanzimat Period of the 19th century, theatre, opera, musical performances and ballrooms became popular in Istanbul. In public places, western-style dance and musical instruments began to be seen.

699fbe74-5142-545f-991c-73824a07527f.name: Author Tevfik Fikret and his book of poetry *Rübab-ı Şikeste*
699fbe74-5142-545f-991c-73824a07527f.short_description: Tevfik Fikret, who published his first book of poetry *Rubab-ı Şikeste* (broken instrument), dealt with love, piety, nature and a worldview that was self-enclosed to the environment. His poems influenced other Turkish poets and he is considered a pioneer of contemporary Turkish poetry. His work also has some seeds of the social opposition of the future.

69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.name: Marius Scalesi
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.short_description: Pictured here is Marius (Mario) Scalesi, a young poet of Italian origin, born on 6 February 1892 in Tunis to an Italian father and a Maltese mother. He suffered from tuberculosis from birth, and became paralysed following a fall down the stairs in his home in La Goulette, the so-called "Little Sicily" of Tunis. Forced to abandon his studies in order to make a living, he completed his education independently. His articles of literary criticism and poems were published in the journal *La Tunisie Illustrée*. His collection of poems, *Les Poèmes d'un Maudit* sheds light on the hardships of his life. He died in 1922 in an asylum in Palermo. A fascinating figure due to his triple cultural identity - Italian, French and Tunisian - he is considered one of the pioneers of North African poetry in French.
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.holder: Institut Culturel Italien (Italian Emabassy in Tunisia)
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
keywords: Marius Scalesi; literature in French; poetry; migration

6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.name: The Bach Hamba brothers
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.short_description: 'Ali (pictured here) and Mohamed were two of the leaders of the protest movement "Harakat al-Shabab al-Tunisi" (the Young Tunisians). Born in Tunis in 1876 and 1881 respectively, these two men of Turkish origin helped found a French-language newspaper, *Le Tunisien*, through which they attacked the politics of the French colonialists and demanded reform. With the help of their comrades, the brothers organised many acts of resistance, such as the Jellaz Affair (1911) and the tramway boycott (1912). The arrest of the majority of the movement's founders, and the suppression of the newspaper *Le Tunisien* marked the end of their activities in Tunisia. However, they continued to make their demands from abroad, working mainly in Geneva and Istanbul, where they finally died in 1818 ('Ali) and 1820 (Mohamed).
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.author: Bechir Yazidi
keywords: Newspaper Le Tunisien; the Young Tunisians movement

6b2642e7-7a75-5343-8798-9e4bf21929a4.name: Luca Petrovich (2nd half of the 19th century – 1900)
6b2642e7-7a75-5343-8798-9e4bf21929a4.short_description: Portrait of Luca Petrovic. He was a commander of Herzegovinian freedom fighters against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.

6c3d3ee7-fba0-54ef-ae3a-b0810a3caeb2.short_description: The bedouin became a symbol of romantic nomadism in the 19th century European imagination. The Zangaki brothers, a pair of Greek photographers working in Egypt, began producing photos of these nomads for Western tourists.
keywords: Bedouins; caravans; nomadism

70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.name: Painting of Vittorio Emanuele II, King of Italy
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.short_description: This oil on canvas portrait from 1862 depicts the King Vittorio Emanuele II (1861–1878). Fair-skinned with blue eyes and brown hair, the king is dressed in official uniform, with a black jacket and silver buttons and a silver belt. The Ordre du Sang, the Nichan al-Dam and the Annunziata medals are on the left of his chest. A royal red cape is draped over his shoulders, bordered by gold decorations, a white fur collar and lapels embellished with black feathers. A gold crown decorated with red and green strasses sits is on his left, and red curtains with tassels and tiebacks in the same colour form the backdrop. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.
70423969-df09-5091-ad7b-50e63c993a4d.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd

70d49b3f-e99f-5946-83f7-c0c3b1092a69.name: Osman Hamdi Bey (During the excavation of Mount Nemrut)
70d49b3f-e99f-5946-83f7-c0c3b1092a69.short_description: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.
keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters,; archaeological excavations

70df1938-c4b1-5bed-9f24-8054cc85bf48.name: Karl I, Emperor of Austria (1887–1922)
70df1938-c4b1-5bed-9f24-8054cc85bf48.short_description: Portrait of Karl I, the last Austrian Emperor. The Austrian and the Ottoman Empires disintegrated after World War I. Karl I had to flee from Austria and died in exile on the island of Madeira.

7445c306-1049-5630-9a00-27983ccbe9b6.name: *Khedive Ismail*
7445c306-1049-5630-9a00-27983ccbe9b6.short_description: Khedive Ismail, the fifth ruler of the Muhammad 'Ali Dynasty, Khedive of Egypt from 1863 to 1879. Ismail assumed rule over Egypt when work on the Suez Canal was ongoing. He continued the project until the Canal was opened for navigation in 1869. He established Dar al-Kutub (the National Library and Archives of Egypt) on 26 September 1870. The First Egyptian Parliament was inaugurated in 1866, during his reign.
keywords: Ruling Family; Rulers of Egypt; The Alawiyya Dynasty; Turks; The Ruling Elite

7503191f-13bf-5090-a965-b30a2948d2bd.name: Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848)
7503191f-13bf-5090-a965-b30a2948d2bd.short_description: Portrait of Ibrahim Pasha (1789–1848). As the best General under his father Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, he fought successfully against the Wahhabites, the Ottoman Army and the Greeks. In 1831 he conquered Syria and governed it until 1841. In 1848 he deposed his senile father and was declared Vice King of Egypt by Sultan Abdülmecid I.
keywords: Ibrahim Pasha; Syria; Greece

75a1a06b-dd6b-5798-a0d2-b2d013063c27.name: Rai Sal Darbari
75a1a06b-dd6b-5798-a0d2-b2d013063c27.short_description: This painting of the Hindu courtier Rai Sal Darbari was once part of the Salim Album, which was assembled during the years 1600 to 1604, for Prince Salim before his accession as the emperor Jahangir. This especially striking depiction of Rai Sal Darbari was surely one of the finest paintings in the album. Immediately noticeable is the palette, with its stunning contrast of rich colours—crimson, ochre and purple—the intensity of which is relieved by the brilliant white of the figure’s turban and one of the *patka*s (sashes) that hangs from his waist. Closer inspection reveals the sensitive treatment of the figure’s face, the fine creases around the eyes and the facial hair, each individual strand of which has been painstakingly rendered.
keywords: miniature painting; illustration; border decoration; calligraphy; portrait; portraiture; textile
materials: Coloured pigments and gold on paper

77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.name: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895)
77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.short_description: Portrait of Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895), who financed the construction of the Suez Canal. Because of the enormous costs of the building and his reform measures, Egypt's debt rose from three million pounds sterling to 100 million pounds sterling. In 1875 Egypt was bankrupt and Ismail Pasha was forced to sell 176,602 shares to Great Britain for 3,976,582 pounds sterling. Egypt came under financial control of France and Great Britain.
keywords: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt; Suez Channel; Emperor Franz Joseph

79b21411-a495-509f-bd1b-4acb4fa78729.name: *Portrait of a Negro*
79b21411-a495-509f-bd1b-4acb4fa78729.description: Morgado de Setúbal, a late 18th-century Portuguese “genre” painter, is quite original in his approach to portraying popular and picturesque scenes. His Portrait and still-life works stand out for their representations of various social types in Portuguese society, where his focus was mainly on the working classes. In this painting he depicts a black slave or servant who wears poorly conserved clothes and points at the viewer. The painting is typical of the artist's use of bold forms and earthy colours.
79b21411-a495-509f-bd1b-4acb4fa78729.short_description: This portrait of a black slave or servant is an example of Portuguese “genre painting”. In his portrayal of popular and picturesque scenes, Morgado de Setúbal allows the viewer to appreciate some late 18th-century Portuguese social types.

7ab5bd97-3948-5e4a-9db2-309afc5b078e.name: A lithographed postcard showing the
7ab5bd97-3948-5e4a-9db2-309afc5b078e.description: The figure is Sharif ʿAwn al-Rafiq Pasha, who served as Sharif and Emir of Mecca from 1882 until his death in 1905. Institutional catalogues of his surviving portrait consistently identify him by this name and term of office. The title, “Sharif of Mecca”, referred to the Hasanid descendants of the Prophet Muhammad who governed Mecca. Sharifian government in the city developed from the tenth century and remained one of the most important institutions of western Hijaz politics for centuries. As a member of the Hashemite ʿAwn household, he governed the holy city, exercised authority connected with the Hajj, and negotiated his position with the Ottoman administration, whose recognition remained essential to the sharifate. The Arabic heading was intended to identify him as "Sharif Makka al-kabir Aun ar-Rafiq"(ʿAwn al-Rafiq, Grand Sharif of Mecca), but the name is irregularly and inaccurately written on the card as "Sharif al-Makka al-kabir Aun ar-Raba".
7ab5bd97-3948-5e4a-9db2-309afc5b078e.bibliography:

Sweis, Sami Jiryis, “Hashemite Household Anxieties: The Amirate of Mecca, Arabism, and the Arab Revolt, 1880–1919”, PhD diss., University of Chicago, 2020.
keywords: Portrait; Mecca, Saudi Arabia; sharifate; government

7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.name: *Woman with mimosa*
7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.short_description: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. In the art of his paintings, he depicted unique details so diligently that he made us recognize our environment and Turkish culture. He illustrated carpets, tile panels, calligraphies, decorative arts, shrines, mosques and human figures in his paintings. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.
7e87a4ee-76a2-59b0-995b-b76a7a6ee825.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters

7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

837581e0-006f-52d2-82bf-795b4cf10463.name: Portrait of Abraham Behor And Nisim Camondo
837581e0-006f-52d2-82bf-795b4cf10463.short_description: Abraham Salomon's descendants, Abraham-Behor (1829-1889) and Nisim (1830-1889) were partners in banking. As a rival to the Ottoman Bank, The Camondo Family established the Ottoman Empire Company-i Umumiyesi (*Societe Generale de l'Empire Ottoman*) with a capital of two million pounds in 1864. Because of the establishment of the Credit General Ottoman Bank in 1868, the Camondo Brothers decided to move the bank to Paris with the idea that the Bank should have absolutely no external links. Abraham-Behor became president of the institution of the *Alliance Israelite Universelle* in 1864. This institution – which instructed students in French in the name of modernization and westernization – was founded to improve the material and spiritual conditions of the Jews and to ensure the spread of education in İstanbul.

83934d9b-77bc-58ef-af02-542c738a2425.name: Portrait of the Marquis of Pombal
83934d9b-77bc-58ef-af02-542c738a2425.description:
The portrait was painted in 1776 by the French artist Louis-Michel van Loo, who was known for his portraits of Kings and noblemen. Van Loo worked from sketches outlined in Lisbon by J. A. Padrão and J. S. Carpinetti, while C. J. Vernet was in charge of the nautical-themed background. Commissioned by the English and Swiss merchants, Gerard Devisme and David Purry, the picture was devised to eulogise the persona and political achievements of the Marquis of Pombal, a central figure in the Age of Enlightenment: a merciless statesman and influential Minister of the Kingdom in the government of José I of Portugal for 27 years (1750–1777).  
The Marquis of Pombal ruled with a heavy hand, suppressing the Jesuits and prevailing over the Portuguese Inquisition and the Church. In the portrait, his left hand gestures toward the River Tagus and Hieronymus Monastery, but also goes further in its propagandist call by encompassing the Kingdom's Atlantic call. Mercantilist, the marquis established the *Junta do Comércio* and other guilds to regulate all commercial activities, favouring trade monopolies run by the merchant bourgeoisie, and impelling the manufacturing business to greater productivity. The marquis rationalised State administration and demarcated the region for the production of Douro and Port wines, guaranteeing the wine's quality trough the *Companhia das Vinhas do Alto Douro*. He also launched the *Aula* *do Comércio* and the *Real Colégio de Nobres;* established the basis for secular public primary schools and in so doing created hundreds of new teaching posts. He reformed the academic curricula of the University of Coimbra, which at the time was inspired by Jesuit teaching.  
The Pombaline reforms, including the reconstruction of Lisbon in the aftermath of the earthquake of 1755, are depicted trough the allegory of Commerce, Arts and Industry seen in the three figures surrounding the statue of King Joseph I, which appears behind the Marquis. The marquis was pragmatic and uncompromising in his efforts to coordinate the rebuilding of downtown Lisbon and the new Praça do Comércio (replacing the old Terreiro do Paço) where the statue of King Joseph I stands. Some of the plans to rebuild Lisbon rest on a table underneath his right arm, and others can be seen on a red walnut carved stool.
83934d9b-77bc-58ef-af02-542c738a2425.short_description: The *Portrait of Marquis de Pombal* was commissioned in 1776 from the French artist Louis Michel van Loo in order to eulogise the persona and political achievements of the Marquis of Pombal, Minister of the Kingdom in the government of José I of Portugal.

83934d9b-77bc-58ef-af02-542c738a2425.obtention: The painting was transferred from the palace of Marquis de Pombal to the Town Hall headquarters in 1939

85ea18f4-df5c-5e4b-ac52-cad7c455e015.name: *The Apotheosis of Emperor Joseph II*
85ea18f4-df5c-5e4b-ac52-cad7c455e015.description:
This small allegorical composition is a rare example of a piece that might have been planned originally purely as a decorative piece. The execution of the painting is finely detailed, and contrary to its small size, it is of exceptional quality. The painting is also unusual in its representation of the emperor, which is not at all in keeping with the normal iconography associated with him.  
The Holy Roman Emperor Joseph II (1765–1790) was King of Hungary from 1780 to 1790. The eldest son of Maria Theresia and Francis von Lorraine, having succeeded to the throne, he tried to organise a unified empire with reforms of Enlightened Absolutism. Both his political and religious policies served the emperor's overall ideal of the strong central power of the state. His reform policies were named after him and are known in Hungary as Josephinism. A limited guarantee of freedom of worship was seen with the Patent of Tolerance in 1781, and he abolished serfdom and the death penalty. Like many of the enlightened monarchs of the time, he was a prolific patron of the arts, commissioning an opera from Mozart and a funeral cantata from the young Beethoven.
85ea18f4-df5c-5e4b-ac52-cad7c455e015.short_description: Because of its small size and compositional form, this painting is a rare example of Baroque allegory associated with the Holy Roman Emperor Joseph II (1765–1790). The painting glorifies the Habsburg emperor and Hungarian king during whose reign Enlightened Absolutism was born. Because of his reforms and the laws he passed, the era is known in Hungary as Josephinism.
85ea18f4-df5c-5e4b-ac52-cad7c455e015.provenance: From the Royal Collection, Royal Palace, Buda
85ea18f4-df5c-5e4b-ac52-cad7c455e015.obtention: Transferred from the Royal Collection, Royal Palace in Buda in 1945
85ea18f4-df5c-5e4b-ac52-cad7c455e015.author: Beatrix Basics
keywords: Enlightenment; Josephinism; allegory; Joseph II Habsburg; Maria Theresia; Franz von Lorraine; panel

8824c22c-0cd4-502b-8da0-b722a3dd6846.name: *Izzedin Yusuf Effendi (1875–1916)*
8824c22c-0cd4-502b-8da0-b722a3dd6846.short_description: Portrait of Izzedin Yusuf Effendi (1875–1916). He was the heir to the throne. In 1916 he committed suicide.

8882d0e5-57fa-5c65-adef-21bc617bd242.name: *Portrait of a Laughing Youth*
8882d0e5-57fa-5c65-adef-21bc617bd242.description:
The painting is mentioned for the first time as part of the collection in the 1693 inventory. It has been attributed variously to different artists in the past, but was confirmed as a “Carracci Caricature” in an 1833 *fideicommissum* (a deed forbidding the heirs to the Borghese estate from splitting up the collection). In the 20th century, it was deemed to be an early work of the Bolognese artist, at a time when Carracci made numerous attempts at “genre works”, leaving some superb examples, such as the famous canvas , *The Beaneater* in the Galleria Colonna, Rome (c. 1583–1584).  
The portrait of the jester has always been thought to be a character from the *Commedia dell'Arte*. This small sketch shows a smiling, mocking youth dressed in a dark suit, ruff and light hat, awkward and upside-down. The supposed jester, with his grotesque red nose, cannot be identified entirely with the theatrical comic tradition and, although the severe and sober clothes resemble the Bolognese mask of “Dottor Graziano”, the unusual hat is perhaps an invention of Carracci himself.  
The light comes from the right, creating a *chiaroscuro* effect on the folds of the hat, emphasising the satisfied look and ambiguous smile of the character, the focal point of the portrait.  
It is the complicit look and smile of a comic actor that, between fiction and reality, skilfully establishes a relationship with the viewer.  
The portrait stands against a simple yellow background, which helps to focus attention on the burlesque face, whose keen, realistic expression is rendered with a sombre palette of colours.  
Free charcoal lines quickly define the sketch, combined with fast, fluid brush strokes. Given the medium (paper on canvas) the use of these tools seems to suggest a desire to capture the immediacy of a live portrait, rather than a caricature, which has been suggested, although this area was of interest to the painter.  
The modernity of expression in the sketch anticipates by half a century the portraits of Velazquez and Bernini and appears to be the beginning of the study of emotions and character types that characterises 18th-century artistic innovation.  
The work is one of Carracci's “small portraits” painted after 1582, where his search for reality was based on simple lines and not precise reproductions of faces.
8882d0e5-57fa-5c65-adef-21bc617bd242.short_description: This piece is an interesting example of the artistic re-invention pursued by Carracci. In his sketchy *Portrait of a Laughing Youth*, dating to around1584, the young artist captures a moment of the youth's laughter. With its spontaneity, it is extraordinarily modern, anticipating the portraits by Bernini and Velázquez 50 years later. It may be the portrait of an actor, the Bolognese mask of the “Dottor Graziano”.
8882d0e5-57fa-5c65-adef-21bc617bd242.obtention: The Borghese Collection was acquired by the Italian State in 1902.

89d4c66b-a374-55e7-8284-7f6b427b03c0.description: This painting by António Ramalho (1859–1916) portrays European fascination for eastern cultures. As well as wearing a Japanese costume, the figure in the painting is surrounded by oriental objects in a clear reference to his aesthetic preferences.

8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.name: ‘Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II (1842–1918)
8a70de1b-8f52-5be5-84b2-f02ae35a3ab5.short_description: Portrait of 'Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II (1842–1918). He was born in 1842 in Istanbul. In 1876 he became Sultan and after the lost war with Russia in 1877, he was forced to agree to the 1878 Congress of Berlin. The signatory powers of the congress allowed Austria to occupy Bosnia-Herzegovina, which belonged to the territory of the Ottoman Empire. In 1888 he had to accept the occupation of Tunisia by France. He tried to modernize the Ottoman Empire with the help of Germany, but in 1908 a revolution of Turkish officers forced him to abdicate. He died in 1918 in Istanbul.
keywords: 'Abd-al-Hamid (Abdülhamid) II; Congress of Berlin; Bosnia-Herzegovina; Tunisia

8aa9aed7-b2ea-50bd-90ad-08ec6d53d8f4.name: Portrait of Émile Prisse d'Avennes dressed in an imitation of the local style
8aa9aed7-b2ea-50bd-90ad-08ec6d53d8f4.short_description: The engineer, painter and architect Prisse d'Avennes (1807–1879) lived in Egypt for 20 years, and was to a great extent assimilated into Egyptian society and had adopted many Egyptian customs. Other figures, such as Delacroix in Morocco and Flaubert in Egypt, were also fascinated by the landscapes, knowledge and customs of these countries, which became the inspiration for many of their works, thus initiating the trend of "Orientalist writing".
keywords: Travelling; Orientalism; Prisee d'Avennes

8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.name: *James Robertson and His Brother-in-Law Felice Beato in Turkish Costume*
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.short_description: A self-portrait of James Robertson and his brother-in-law Felice Beato standing side by side and dressed in Turkish costume is an important work in the history of photography. This picture is in every sense a coloured counterpart of two other portrait photographs by Robertson first brought to light by Bahattin Öztuncay in 1991. The image of Felice Beato in this identical photograph is the only known picture of him in his youth.
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
keywords: self-portrait; watercolour on photographs; Felice Beato

8c4762e1-5805-5789-8cac-3fcdc7d7a021.name: *Portrait of a Sculptor – Gottfried Fritsch*
8c4762e1-5805-5789-8cac-3fcdc7d7a021.description:
A slightly stooped male half-figure emerges from a dark background, in which the viewer can make out roughly worked stones. While his expressive look scans the viewer, the man, holding a pair of compasses in his left hand, leans against a sculpture in progress representing a human figure. The clothes (a casually open shirt, fur hat), the statue and the tool are attributes that characterise the person depicted as an artist-sculptor. The lower section of the picture has probably been cut off at some point: the sculptor's fingers touch the canvas edge and the palm of the statue surfaces suddenly at the bottom-right of the trunk, without logical connection.  
The composition is diagonally balanced; the light accents of the white shirt and the body are supplemented by the colour contrast of the green coat and its pink lining.  
During the Baroque period artists were frequently represented as art connoisseurs, collectors of antiques and court artists with characteristic attributes, whereas before they had been regarded as mere craftsmen.  
Gottfried Fritsch (1706–1750), the last classical Baroque sculptor in Moravia, is depicted as a *virtuosus quondam statuarius*, a learned artist. The picture comes from the Tovačov chateau, owned by the Petřvaldskýs of Petřvald in the 18th century. Count Amand Antonín oversaw from Tovačov a demesne in which he initiated important artistic activities. Among other things, he enabled Fritsch to study sculpture in Vienna and Italy. The sculptor decorated the Petřvaldskýs' graveyard in Střílky.  
Franz Anton Palko, who also worked as a painter for the Bishop of Olomouc, stayed in Brno where he created the altarpiece for the parish Church of St. James. František Vavřinec Korompay, a renowned artist, was one of his students. Palko's benefactors and patrons included Count Wenzel Anton Kaunitz-Rietberg, State Chancellor of the Habsburg monarchy. The count particularly admired the artist's “French” portrait style.
8c4762e1-5805-5789-8cac-3fcdc7d7a021.short_description: The picture represents “a learned artist”, a sculptor-virtuoso. The “French-style” portrait was created for the Lord of Petřvald, a significant supporter of the arts. The painter was one of the most acknowledged portraitists of the period and was also active in the imperial court in Vienna.
8c4762e1-5805-5789-8cac-3fcdc7d7a021.initial_owner: Amand Anton Petřvaldský of Petřvald, Střílky
8c4762e1-5805-5789-8cac-3fcdc7d7a021.method_for_datation: The high quality of the picture, its colour scheme and layout invite comparison with *Portrait of Father* from 1746 (Belvedere, Wien), *Self-portrait with a Broad-brimmed Hat* and *Portrait of Count* *Unwerth* (Szépművészeti Múzeum, Budapest).
8c4762e1-5805-5789-8cac-3fcdc7d7a021.obtention: An inventory made after Amand Petřvaldský of Petřvald's death in 1762 contains and entry: *Porträt den Bildhauer Fritsch vorstellend, in einem Rahme*. The picture was originally found in Střílky Chateau and later in Tovačov Chateau; it then became the property of the Künburgs. In 1946 it became part of the picture collection at Brno Museum. It has been in the Moravian Gallery, Brno since 1961.

8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.name: *Le général Khaireddine* (painting)
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.short_description: This 1852 oil on canvas by Simil depicts the General Khaireddine (Khayr al-Din) on horseback in official uniform. This brigadier-general uniform from the latter half of the 19th century comprises a full suit, a short coat, a shirt, a checia, a chemla and a pair of shoes. The brigadier-general also wore two crossed capes and a sword, with the Nichan al-Iftikhar (1st class) medal on the right-hand side of the chest, next to the insignas, and the Légion d'Honneur and the Ordre des Saints Maurice et Lazare medals on the left-hand side.

8d0345df-1e22-5450-8f37-706dc5be7d91.name: A Woman from Cairo
8d0345df-1e22-5450-8f37-706dc5be7d91.short_description: This photo from Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was taken by the Florentine naturalist during his travels around the world in 1865 and 1868 while advancing diplomatic and commercial relations between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

8d7fb33a-5d98-5c0b-a5f1-fab6b28e82f7.name: Painting of Mohamed Sadok Bey and Napoléon III
8d7fb33a-5d98-5c0b-a5f1-fab6b28e82f7.short_description: This oil on canvas by Alexandre Debelle shows Mohamed Sadok Bey seeing off the emperor Napoléon III as he leaves Algiers on 20 September 1860. The bey and the emperor are on horseback, surrounded by their garrisons and local inhabitants in traditional dress. This painting is set in an urban dwelling by the sea, and the tricolour French flag is fluttering above the crowds. The bey is dressed in official uniform, with the Nichan al-Ahd round his next, and the Nichan al-Dam, the diamond-crusted Légion d'Honneur and the Nichan al-Iftikhar (with the eagle of the Second Empire) medals are on the left side of his chest. This painting is evidence of an active diplomatic relationship between the Palais du Bardo and the European chancelleries.
8d7fb33a-5d98-5c0b-a5f1-fab6b28e82f7.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd

8df53ce3-81e5-5c23-89d6-2324283cfe08.name: *Portrait of Provost Augustinus Aurelius*
8df53ce3-81e5-5c23-89d6-2324283cfe08.description: The composition is typical of portraits of High Church representatives. The provost of the Augustinian monastery in Šternberk is portrayed at the age of 50 sitting in an upholstered armchair with gilded carving, against a background of a green curtain and a decorative vase with the monastery's emblem. The shape and colours of the drapery create a dynamic spiral movement adding to the portrait's effect. Augustinus Aurelius is dressed in ceremonial clothing, a white soutane, white surplice and blue almuca, holding a blue cap in his left hand. The attributes of his position in the church also appear: a mitre, sceptre and a crucifix around his neck. With his right hand, the provost points to the plans for the Výšovice residence which was, together with the completion and decoration of the Šternberk Church, among the provost's major building enterprises where he favoured a plain classical style. The provost's diary has survived containing an entry on a performance given by the young Mozart in Brno in December 1767. The provost may have met Korompay on this occasion and commissioned him with the portrait. Although Korompay was a renowned portraitist in his time only a handful of portraits of this type have survived. The provost's portrait was inspired by František Antonín Palko, said to have been the artist's teacher. Korompay's craftsmanship is evident in the finely rendered lace of the attire and its ornamentation. Colour harmony, fine, light, modelling of shapes, and the rendering of the provost's soulful expression, manifest the skill of an artist obviously influenced by Martin Meytens's court portraits and French models.
8df53ce3-81e5-5c23-89d6-2324283cfe08.short_description: The composition is typical of portraits of High Church representatives. Colour harmony, fine, light, modelling of shapes, and the rendering of the provost’s expression, manifest the skill of an artist obviously influenced by the court portraits of František Antonín Palko and Martin Meytens.
8df53ce3-81e5-5c23-89d6-2324283cfe08.method_for_datation: The picture is marked on the reverse: *Reverendissmus et amplissimus Dominus Aurelius Augustin, natus 18 Januari 1719, electus die 16. 8df53ce3-81e5-5c23-89d6-2324283cfe08.obtention: The picture, intended for the hall of an Augustinian residence in Výšovice, is on long-term loan to the Moravian Gallery, Brno.

8e204732-2316-5b8b-bd49-13709f67292e.name: Minto Album
8e204732-2316-5b8b-bd49-13709f67292e.short_description: The Minto Album is a collection of forty, now loose folios, divided between the Chester Beatty Library (nineteen) and the Victoria and Albert Museum, London (twenty-one). It includes some of the finest Mughal paintings ever produced and consists mainly of standing portraits of emperors and other individuals important at court. The paintings included here depict Jahangir (r. 1605–27) holding a globe, Shah Jahan (r. 1627–58) in an orange robe, Shah Jahan and his sons, Mu‘in al-Din Chisti, spiritual guide of the Mughals, and a religious scholar identified by inscription as Muhammad Riza Kashmiri. The magnificent floral borders that surround each painting are as impressive as the paintings themselves.
keywords: album; portrait; portraiture; court; royal; emperor; illumination; allegory; prince; sufism; saint; scholar; religion; floral decoration; angel; crown
materials: Coloured pigments and gold on paper

8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.name: *Algerians*
8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.short_description: This study consists of a series of sketches depicting various Algerians. The subjects are mostly women, whose faces, wrapped in a traditional *haik*, are particularly interesting. According to experts only two paintings of this kind exist today. Before being acquired by the museum this study belonged to an important collection from the late 19th century. In 2003 it was published in the Australian scholar Roger Benjamin's collection dedicated to Auguste Renoir's Algerian period, *Renoir and Algeria*.
8eb7973a-8c9e-5910-83bd-ad5e77872aba.author: Dalila Orfali

8ec0ecf7-b1a9-5b83-9f8a-0dc7cfe15831.name: *Portrait of Tommaso Campeggi and his Family*
8ec0ecf7-b1a9-5b83-9f8a-0dc7cfe15831.description:
This painting formerly credited to the Lombard painter Pier Francesco Cittadini, has been recently reattributed to the Bolognese painter Lorenzo Pasinelli (1998). The portrait is characterised by the presence of such Nordic elements as the dark background and the analytical description of the 12 people. Pasinelli probably painted the great canvas during his stay in Rome, as a present for his host Tommaso Campeggi, the ambassador of Bologna to the Holy See. In 1666 it was moved to the palace owned by Tommaso Campeggi in via San Mamolo, in Bologna. When the house was sold the picture was moved to the residence of “Strà San Donato” and finally to the castle of Dozza, the Campeggi country residence.  
It is one of the rare examples of group portraits in Bolognese baroque painting. The impression is that of an austere and somewhat provincial aristocracy. They are not concerned with being carefully examined by the painter and only interested in portraiture for its social implications. The family is sitting in the traditional scheme, following a hierarchical order and rigidly divided in two groups, males and females. The first born is given central position, next to his sisters who are holding his gloves. Tommaso is the most static and affected figure with rigid authoritarianism, whilst the elegance of the clothes is more emphasized in the female figures.
8ec0ecf7-b1a9-5b83-9f8a-0dc7cfe15831.short_description: The painting depicts the entire Campeggi family. The result is a perfectly balanced mixture of Bolognese and northern features combined with compositional and technical skill.

8f10719a-7586-5524-9036-a47811acc887.short_description: Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, founder of Modern Egypt and Wali of Egypt in 1805. He was the head of the Alawiyya Dynasty that ruled Egypt from 1805 to 1952, and founder of modern Egypt. He came to Egypt in 1799 as part of a military unit to fight with the Turks – and the help of the British – to drive the French out of Egypt. However, the Turkish forces were defeated in 1799 in the Battle of Abu Qir.

905cb8f2-54fa-520a-b0bc-209a26809787.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
905cb8f2-54fa-520a-b0bc-209a26809787.short_description: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in 19th century. Vassilaki Kargopoulo was of Greek descent. His first studio was opened in 1850 near the Russian Consulate. Between the years of 1859 and 1860, he began to attract the attention of customers from all sections of society. He focused on Ottoman clothing and street vendors in 1860.

91b66b55-0c91-5d46-b3bc-af6121a29639.name: Portrait of Mihai Suţu
91b66b55-0c91-5d46-b3bc-af6121a29639.short_description: Mihai Suţu was the last Greek prince of Moldova. The Sublime Porte imposed Greek rulers in Wallachia and Moldavia (called “Phanariotes” because they came from Fanar, the Greek neighborhood of Istanbul) at the beginning of the 18th century and maintained them until 1821. During this period some modernizing reforms, influenced by the ideology of the Occidental Enlightenment, were introduced in the Romanian countries. The drawing was made by French artist Louis Dupré, who visited Greece, Istanbul, the Balkan Peninsula and the Near East in 1819 –1820. In the summer of 1819 he arrived in Bucharest together with Mihail Şuţu, whom he had met in Istanbul. He painted Şuţu laying on a red divan, wearing Oriental clothes.

921bd231-072a-5b12-b6bf-ef1ef9ab5517.name: Metal plaque from India
921bd231-072a-5b12-b6bf-ef1ef9ab5517.short_description: This Indian metal plaque depicts Jahangir Shah, the fourth Mughal emperor. It had two inscriptions in Persian: the first reads "Daylight of the country, year 1013” and the second, golden inscription on the upper left side reads "Lord Jahangir, the Emperor." The plate is decorated with small frames in which verses of a poem about the Emperor are inscribed. The beginning and end of the poem are missing, suggesting that there may have been other objects of the same kind bearing the rest of the poem. The poem recounts a discussion between the Emperor and a proxy.
keywords: Mughal; Jahangir; Metalwork

92891afc-502b-5609-8db7-99bf7bb50e6c.name: Franz Joseph I, Emperor of Austria (1830–1916)
92891afc-502b-5609-8db7-99bf7bb50e6c.short_description: Portrait of Emperor Franz Joseph as an officer of the *Kaiserjäger* (Elite regiment). He ruled Austria for 68 years. During his long reign he had cordial relation to the Sultans of the Ottoman Empire and visited Istanbul and Jerusalem. He died in 1916 during World War I.

92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.name: Photograph of Krste Petkov Misirkov with his friends
92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.short_description: Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) is the author of the book “On Macedonian Matters”, which was published in Sofia in 1903. 9438f959-d105-5cd5-890f-56a9cdcc3715.short_description: Portrait of Josef Freiherr Philippovich-Philippsberg (1818–1889). In 1836 Philippovich-Philippsberg joined the Austrian Army. 96a0b74f-0971-56c3-8154-0b603d6d4116.name: *Portrait of Emperor Joseph II and His Second Wife Marie Josepha of Bavaria and Counts Esterházy, Bathiany and Liechtenstein*
96a0b74f-0971-56c3-8154-0b603d6d4116.alternate_name: *Joseph II with Wife Maria Josepha of Bavaria, Close Courtiers and Ladies-in-Waiting*
96a0b74f-0971-56c3-8154-0b603d6d4116.description:
A counterpart to this sizeable canvas is the picture *Maria Theresa with Sons Below the Bust of Her Deceased Husband Franz Stephan of Lorraine and Chancellor Kounic-Rietberg*. This painting represents the hierarchy of both the dynasty and the monarchy. After the death of his father, Joseph II ruled side-by-side with Maria Theresa. In the background, Josef Wenzl of Liechtenstein indicates a medallion bearing a portrait of Isabela of Parma, Joseph II's first wife. On the right, behind the throne, Joseph's two unmarried sisters, Marie Elisabeth and Marie Anna, are engaged in conversation. In the foreground stands Franz Esterházy with a tiger skin, while Count Karl Josef Batthyány, High Steward, is located at the edge of the canvas. The festive air is enhanced by the arrangement of a drapery with golden tassels together with the seating of the figures on the steps. The landscape in the background features an obelisk topped with a globe upon which an eagle perches holding in its beak a curled serpent biting its own tail a symbol of eternity. The eagle, a creature associated with Jupiter, was among the attributes of imperial iconography and refers to the sovereign's virtues. Another attribute and a symbol of wisdom is the shield with the head of Medusa at the bottom of the picture, on a stone vase. A group of *putti* taming a lion in the upper section of the vase symbolise the power of love and its victory over physical strength.  
The group portrait was commissioned by the abbot of the Premonstratensian Monastery in Louka near Znojmo as an expression of loyalty. The paintings come from the summer refectory, a key section of the monastery designed as a “Temple of Solomon”. The major decorative components were paintings by Franz Anton Maulbertsch depicting essential elements of the Premonstratensian order. These were accompanied by a series of portraits of monastery supporters and superiors.
96a0b74f-0971-56c3-8154-0b603d6d4116.short_description: The group allegorical portrait of the Habsbourg family was commissioned by the abbot of the Premonstratensian Monastery in Louka near Znojmo – one of the most important monasteries in the Danubian country – as an expression of loyalty. The painting represents the hierarchy of both the dynasty and the monarchy.
96a0b74f-0971-56c3-8154-0b603d6d4116.method_for_datation: Palko did a sketch for the picture of Maria Theresa known from a replica by Josef Winterhalder Jr. After Palko’s untimely death, the two paintings were finished by Anton Glunck, a graduate of the Vienna Academy. Glunck is also mentioned as the artist of the pictures in the inventory of the monastery collated by Josef Winterhalder Jr., who also supplemented it with drawn records. Glunck’s participation is confirmed by three receipts preserved in the Moravian Provincial Archive.
96a0b74f-0971-56c3-8154-0b603d6d4116.obtention: The picture comes from the summer refectory of the Premonstratensian Monastery in Louka near Znojmo. When the monastery was dissolved in 1784 the picture became the property of Count Waldorf in Sádek, near Třebíč, until 1904. It was then owned by Count Chorinský and found in the Veselí na Moravě Chateau. After the Second World War the picture came into the possession of the State Chateau, Valtice.

97284ed3-c2ab-51af-8cd2-2ae8ea41f09e.name: *Portrait of the Beneficiary Faustino das Neves*
97284ed3-c2ab-51af-8cd2-2ae8ea41f09e.description:
Strongly influenced by her father, Baltazar Gomes Figueira, and by painters such as Francisco Zurbarán, Juan de Roelas and Daniel Seghers, Josefa de Ayala worked in a small provincial centre outside Lisbon. Away from the court, and in a place where the medieval lifestyle was preserved, she related to the politics opposed to the Spanish Habsburg dynasty, supporting the Restoration cause of the Royal House of Braganza. The social life of this micro-society revolved around social gatherings and meetings in convents and noble residences. The noblemen – members of the Municipal Senate – religious orders, brotherhood and charitable institutions with whom she fraternized, were well-read and had no economic restrictions. In their homes were many works of art some of which were commissioned from local provincial artists.  
From as early as the 17th century, Josefa had several biographies written about her. Costa Meesen (1696) referred to her “cleanliness and aptitude” upon imitating “things from nature”. Writer Damião Froes Perym (1736) also praises her “skill, beauty, honesty and charm” and her moral virtues. In the 19th century, José Silvestre Seabra and Almeida Garrett made reference to *Portrait of the Beneficiary Faustino das Neves*, considering it the genre which best revealed the sensitive side of Josefa d'Óbidos. The piece got lost in time and in 1957 it was identified by Reis-Santos as the work of Josefa d'Óbidos.  
The artist perfectly captures the psychology of this distinguished man from Óbidos. His dark clothing and his vigorous look contrast with the luminosity of the white and beige of his face, accentuating the Counter-Reformation features of the piece. The male figure, accompanied by an angel announcing his death, is purposely decentralised relative to the axis of the composition. This is a peculiarity which enhances the formal skills of Josefa de Ayala thus allowing her to be included within the ranks of the best 17th-century Portuguese painters.
97284ed3-c2ab-51af-8cd2-2ae8ea41f09e.short_description: Josefa de Ayala skilfully conveys the psychology through the glance, gesture and pose of this distinguished man from the town of Óbidos. His dark clothing and vigorous look contrast with the luminosity provided by the white and beige tones of his face. The figure is accompanied by an angel announcing his death.

98465502-2fc0-537f-8943-a5b60d87d5c5.name: Osman Hamdi Bey (Getting mold of Antiochus relief During the excavation of Mount Nemrut)
98465502-2fc0-537f-8943-a5b60d87d5c5.short_description: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.
keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters; archaeological excavations

9863f692-894f-5cb2-b496-b0ec25aba740.name: Kabyle mother with her child
9863f692-894f-5cb2-b496-b0ec25aba740.short_description: Western photographers were particularly interested in both women's daily lives, and family life. This photo from 1920 shows a Kabyle woman carrying her baby with a look of pride on her face.

9c39a32f-844c-5e79-9249-d24aa6612ad5.name: Siamese diplomatic service
9c39a32f-844c-5e79-9249-d24aa6612ad5.short_description: in 1861, Mongkut, the King of Siam, sent a diplomatic service to Paris, not in order to create an alliance, but to preserve their independence by sending messages of good will to various European sovereigns. Napoléon III organised a lavish reception at the Palais Fontainebleau, recalling the Siamese reception which Louis XIV received in 1684. This photo reveals the importance of the Siamese delegation (three ambassadors and ten attachés in their military dress) accompanied by the Abbot Larnaudie, interpreter for the Siamese court.
keywords: Diplomacy; colonies; Siam; France

9d9c9b21-26f5-5feb-9433-34771e40c124.name: Nikola Karev
9d9c9b21-26f5-5feb-9433-34771e40c124.short_description: Nikola Karev (1877–1905) was one of the ideological leaders and organizers of the Uprising of Ilinden. The uprising broke out on the night of 2 August 1903. After taking over, Krushevo revolutionaries declared the Krushevo Republic on 3 August. The Headquarters of the uprising took the military control over the town. The other governing bodies were the Revolutionary Council, consisting of sixty of the most prominent citizens representing all nationalities, and the Government, consisting of six members. Vangel Dinu was the Prime Minister and Nikola Karev was the President of the Republic. Owing to the progressive socialist ideas of Nikola Karev and other revolutionaries, the Krushevo Republic was laid on truly democratic foundations and republican principles. Karev announced the Krushevo Manifesto as a truly democratic document addressing all nationalities living in Macedonia, regardless of their religion, envisioning equal rights for everyone.
9d9c9b21-26f5-5feb-9433-34771e40c124.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
keywords: Revolutionary Council; Government

9ece1ead-7c0b-528b-bdd1-e15c148b868c.name: Medallion
9ece1ead-7c0b-528b-bdd1-e15c148b868c.short_description:
In Rome in the 4th century, glass-makers fully exploited the technique of sandwiched gold glass. Religious subjects - predominantly Christian but also Jewish - as well as portraits of families and individuals such as this piece were depicted in gold leaf with stippled and painted decoration. This was then placed between two layers of colourless glass that were fused together.  
  
The identity of the man in this portrait is not known, but the costly process of this technique means it was somebody of high status. Medallions formed by this method were sometimes made as decorative pendants for wearing, but most were set into the base of bowls and dishes to commemorate a special occasion or present as a wedding gift. The portrait disks were later broken out of the dishes to be re-used as grave markers.

9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.name: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895)
9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.short_description: Portrait of Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895), who financed the construction of the Suez Canal. Because of the enormous costs of the building and his reform measures, Egypt's debt rose from three million pounds sterling to 100 million pounds sterling. In 1875 Egypt was bankrupt and Ismail Pasha was forced to sell 176,602 shares to Great Britain for 3,976,582 pounds sterling. Egypt came under financial control of France and Great Britain.
keywords: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt; Suez Channel; Great Britain

9faeadc1-e075-5681-bdc1-072dabd412c6.name: Miniature 'Wine-Server' ('Portrait of a Young Man')
9faeadc1-e075-5681-bdc1-072dabd412c6.short_description: According to the inscription in the lower left corner of the composition, the author of the painting is Reza Abbasi, the most prominent Iranian artist of the AD 17th century. The founder of the new style of painting and the head of the famous Isfahan school, Reza Abbasi has departed from the bright decorative colours of the classic Persian miniature and turned to a more restrained and unusual palette. He chose a thin and sensitive calligraphic line as his main means of expression. Wine-server (Persian: *saqi*) - a young man who served at banquets, pouring wine to guests. A flask in a form of a gourd in his right hand testifies to his role. The man is dressed in a malachite green robe. An orange silk scarf is untied and carelessly thrown over his shoulders. His full face, dreamy staring eyes, curls falling down on cheeks, small gentle hands and graceful posture, the smooth curves of which seem to echo the flexible lines of plants - all correspond to the traditional type of an effeminate youth-*saqi*.
9faeadc1-e075-5681-bdc1-072dabd412c6.method_for_datation: Stylistic analysis and inscription reading by V. Krachkovskaya (publication, 1926, origin and date).

a0dc5e60-a3ed-58a3-8317-2db79e5cbc80.name: Mico Liubibratic (1839–1889)
a0dc5e60-a3ed-58a3-8317-2db79e5cbc80.short_description: Portrait of Mico Liubibratic. He was a commander of Herzegovinian freedom fighters against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.
keywords: Mico Liubibratic; Congress of Berlin; Bosnia-Herzegovina

a12c9928-1d6f-5b1e-814c-74692d5b8de6.name: Arabi, Sayed Ahmed Pasha (1841–1911)
a12c9928-1d6f-5b1e-814c-74692d5b8de6.short_description: Portrait of minister Sayed Ahmed Pasha Arabi (Urabi). In 1882, the war minister took power in Egypt and demanded an end to the financial control imposed by the UK and France. This led to an intervention by the British Navy under Admiral Seymour, who defeated the Egyptian army.
keywords: Urabi; Arabi; Egypt

a532878c-9737-5402-a686-e8febd96a222.name: *Klemens Wenzel Lother of Metternich-Winneburg (1773–1859)*
a532878c-9737-5402-a686-e8febd96a222.short_description: Klemens Wenzel Lothar of Metternich was the leading diplomat at the Congress of Vienna (1815) who organized the balance of power between the European states. The core of Metternich's policy was supporting Austrian hegemony in Italy and preventing Russian hegemony in Germany. In the German Confederation, there existed an equilibrium between Austria and Prussian influences. Metternich's so-called "balance of power" politics ensured peace in Central Europe for a generation.

a7c102ce-f4bb-5330-8383-c17696408f62.name: Khayr al-Din Pacha
a7c102ce-f4bb-5330-8383-c17696408f62.short_description: Khayr al-Din Pacha brought in many reforms which significantly changed the precolonial period, to a great extent Westernizing the Beylik of Tunis, which was later portrayed as "modernization". This Mamluk of circasian origin was probably born in 1825, and came to Tunis as a child in 1840. He quickly climbed the ranks and took his father-in-law Mustapha Khaznadar's place as Chief Minister under the rule of Mohamed Sadok Bey from 1873 to 1877. He died in 1890 in Istanbul, where he had served as grand vizier. He appears tall and majestic in this photograph, and carries authority in his piercing gaze. His jacket is richly decorated, bearing the coat of arms of the sovereign who bought him and brought him to Tunis, Ahmed Bey (1835–1855).

acc57934-ae32-5e43-8f31-305447337577.name: Water pumping equipment in Kağıthane, Istanbul
acc57934-ae32-5e43-8f31-305447337577.short_description: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. Cendere Hamidian Water Pump Station was built by Abdülhamid II in 1902 at an altitude of 34 metres above sea level. With its function, architectural design and mechanical equipment, the station is a unique monument to the history of the architecture industry in the Ottoman Empire. It pumped to Balmumcu and Beşiktaş – in the direction of Tophane, moving water coming from 20 different pipes in Kağıthane using steam pump machines.
