ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.name: *Sorolla in Tetouan*
ef67fa8c-4ff1-55bf-83f3-ae6118113aaa.description:
This picture was taken in Tetouan during a trip of the painter Joaquín Sorolla and his friends to Morocco in 1919. Sorolla's family and friends were portrayed with local people, a highlight of which is the Moor Selam and other characters and exotic animals, such as the monkey. Especially interesting is her daughter Helena who appeared in a Moorish costume.  
This travel appeared in the newspapers El Confidencial and ABC which also published this photograph.  
This family trip brought back memories and objects. The painter's daughter, Helena, had their little Moorish corner on the stairs of the house which is now the Sorolla Museum. A table, a chest, tambourines, fabrics, jewellery were bought back as souvenirs.

f02e2658-e5a5-5c73-8f21-a84aea27d4e2.name: Osman Hamdi Bey (During the excavation of Lagina, together with French archaeologists Cammonard and Cartier)
f02e2658-e5a5-5c73-8f21-a84aea27d4e2.short_description: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.

f03b716a-a1e0-58f0-b452-2c2a089e34f2.name: Members of Court of Sultan Selim II Mounted as an Album Leaf
f03b716a-a1e0-58f0-b452-2c2a089e34f2.short_description: From the late sixteenth century until the formation of the Republic of Turkey in 1922, the Ottoman sultans maintained a strong tradition of imperial portraiture. Influenced by European oil painting and Persian miniatures, Ottoman portraits provide important information about court ceremonies, changing fashions, and members of the court. The right side of a double-page composition, this painting was created as a pendant to a portrait of Selim II (r. Hegira 974-982/1566-1574) on the left, now in the collection of the Aga Khan Museum, Toronto. The musicians, servants, and courtiers, who are identified by their inscriptions, face left, toward the sultan, in a show of deference to their ruler. Taken together the pair of paintings depict a *majlis* scene reflecting the pleasure-oriented atmosphere of Selim’s court. It is possible that the figure of the court jester at far right is a self-portrait of the artist.
f03b716a-a1e0-58f0-b452-2c2a089e34f2.holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
f03b716a-a1e0-58f0-b452-2c2a089e34f2.method_for_datation: Less formal than official Ottoman royal depictions, this painting (and its pendant) was likely made prior to Selim’s ascension to the throne in 1566 and was probably produced during his time as a prince governing Kütahya. Several of the figures depicted with captions can be further identified as boon companions of Selim II, one of whom, Turak Çelabi, died in 1561-62, suggesting a terminus ante quem for the work.
f03b716a-a1e0-58f0-b452-2c2a089e34f2.method_for_provenance: It is signed “Nigari, slave of Sultan Selim Khan.” Nigari was the pseudonym used by the famed Turkish navigator Haydar Reis, who was also well-known as a portrait painting under Sultan Suleyman and his son and successor Selim II.

f0e2d598-8e69-5768-bd25-d9db967e1292.name: Painting Entitled ‘al-Rihlah al-Hijaziyyah/ Sacred Pilgrimage Journey’
f0e2d598-8e69-5768-bd25-d9db967e1292.description: According to a plaque below the images, the painting depicts the pilgrimage of ‘Abbas Hilmi II, the Khedive of Egypt, which he performed in 1909. His portrait is on the left; on the right is that of Mehmed V Rashad, the contemporary Ottoman sultan. To the left and right of the Ka‘bah, which occupies the centre of the painting, are depictions of the Mosque of the Prophet in Medina and the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem. Many of the remaining images are based on photographs of the hajj published in the July 1953 issue of National Geographic.

f10531b4-c48a-52e3-ba7a-d83cfa1d0403.name: Portrait of Cardinal Prospero Lambertini
f10531b4-c48a-52e3-ba7a-d83cfa1d0403.description:
In 1739, Cardinal Prospero Lambertini, the Archbishop of Bologna sat for a grand portrait in the studio of the painter Giuseppe Maria Crespi. The following year, he became Pope Benedict XIV and asked the painter to insert the papal attributes into the portrait. The painting was sent to the Vatican Picture Gallery in Rome where it remains today.  
This portrait, often assumed to be a sketch, is actually a small-scale replica painted by the artist as a souvenir of the first version. The cardinal, with his round jolly face is depicted near his writing table rising to his feet with a pen in his hand. He is literally surrounded by books, a living presence in his studio. This atmosphere of cordiality and lively immediacy vanishes in the Vatican portrait, Crespi portrays the pope clad in gravity. Benedict XIV was a wise and learned man, with a deep knowledge of scientific culture. He was attached to his native town and worked hard to promote intense growth of the University of Bologna (Studio) and of other cultural institutions. He also strove to accelerate the completion of the cathedral.
f10531b4-c48a-52e3-ba7a-d83cfa1d0403.short_description: This painting is considered to be a small size replica of the official portrait of Cardinal Prospero Lambertini, Archbishop of Bologna, portrayed by Giuseppe Maria Crespi before he was pope (Benedict XIV), in 1740. After the election the painter added to the portrait the papal attributes and sent it to Rome. Now the picture is held in the Pinacoteca Vaticana. It is likely Crespi made a small replica before making the changes in order to keep a souvenir of the original portrait.
f10531b4-c48a-52e3-ba7a-d83cfa1d0403.method_for_datation: We have no direct evidence about this particular picture. Luigi Crespi, son of the painter Giuseppe Maria, in his additions to the *Felsina Pittrice* (1796) tells the story of the official portrait, now in the Vatican Museums. Today, letters remain in the Vatican Archives between the painter and the Secretary of State of the Pope regarding the invoice to Rome.

f2d5cedb-276c-5bcc-adf8-742a01444f80.name: A Woman from Cairo
f2d5cedb-276c-5bcc-adf8-742a01444f80.short_description: This photo from Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was collected by the Florentine naturalist while travelling the world between 1865 through 1868 as he advanced diplomatic and commercial affairs between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

f36b7d3e-8e7a-5356-9555-d10076d72a09.name: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892)
f36b7d3e-8e7a-5356-9555-d10076d72a09.short_description: Portrait of Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892). After the deposition of his father Ismail Pasha, Muhammad Tawfiq took over the government in Egypt. The Arabi revolution diminished his power radically. In 1882 he asked for help from Great Britain. British troops suppressed the Arabi revolution and occupied Egypt. Muhammad Tawfiq became ruler at the grace of the British government.

f4070107-bd84-5299-8132-72ae7c8a76e8.name: *Portrait of Felice Zacchia Rondanini*
f4070107-bd84-5299-8132-72ae7c8a76e8.description:
Domenico Guidi, nephew of the sculptor Giuliano Finelli, with whom he worked in Naples (1639–49), moved to the workshops of Algardi in Rome in 1649. He stayed there until the death of his master, from whom he learned the classicism that is a fundamental part of his style, although he was not as skilled in its execution.  
The bust was acquired by the Italian state from an antique market in 1907. It was initially attributed to the Berninian school on account of the elliptical shape enclosing the female figure and the “unfinished” back, a trait peculiar to Bernini on unseen surfaces. It was later attributed to 17th- and 18th-century sculptors (such as Bracci on account of the stylistic analogies with the sculptor's bust of Clement XII in the Borghese collection). It was finally attributed to Guidi, who was summoned by Bernini in 1668 to decorate the Ponte Sant'Angelo, although his style was more classical and less elaborate in form.  
The woman is probably Felice Zacchia Rondanini, daughter of Laudivio Zacchia who, once widowed, gave his life to religion and was made a cardinal in 1626. Algardi made a portrait of the father, having already made several busts for the Rondanini family. For his part, Guidi was responsible for the Rondanini tomb in S. Maria del Popolo, Rome in 1657. In 1683, in the same church, he sculpted the funerary monument to Vincenza Danesi, who some scholars connect to the Borghese portrait, although there is no documentation to support the theory. A ring is fixed under the cloak, which suggests it was originally intended to be placed in a niche, and the measurements coincide with the anchor points of the Danesi monument.  
The old lady wears a large veil forming a convex shape, on which shadows accentuate the face in the foreground, which is struck by light. The detail on the face is particularly interesting, especially the deep lines on the face and neck and the wart on the right cheek, emphasising the realism of the portrait.  
Guidi was so well regarded by the French for his classicism that by the end of his career he was a synonym for French taste. Nonetheless, a sculptural group made for Louis XIV failed to please the king and it ended up in the same place as Bernini's: the gardens of Versailles.
f4070107-bd84-5299-8132-72ae7c8a76e8.short_description:
A portrait of an old lady who wears a veil. The detail on the face is particularly interesting, especially the deep lines on the face and neck and the wart on the right cheek, emphasising the realism of the portrait.  
Guidi produced a few works for Bernini (such as the *Angel with a Lance* on Ponte Sant'Angelo) most of his collaborative work was, however, with Algardi.

f6a973df-a6b0-51b8-8bb0-fd4026b06319.name: Photograph of Ion Ghica (sitting)
f6a973df-a6b0-51b8-8bb0-fd4026b06319.short_description: In 1848, Ion Ghica was the envoy of the Wallachian revolutionaries to Istanbul, where he remained after the suppression of the revolution. He created connections among the Ottoman officials, being appreciated by Reshid-Pasha (Grand Vizier from 1854), and became a supporter of the Romanian Principalities’ union under Ottoman sovereignty. A former journalist, he devised the project (not realized) for an economic and literary periodical, published in all the languages spoken in the Empire. In 1854 he was appointed governor of the island of Samos, where he took measures against piracy and founded several schools (a middle school, an agricultural school, a marine school and a girls’ institute). His activity earned him the title of “prince”(bey) of Samos, which he received from sultan Abdülmecid in February 1856.

fac6052d-8778-5973-8864-63b61123c63f.name: *Portrait of Baroness Erzsébet Haller*
fac6052d-8778-5973-8864-63b61123c63f.description:
*Portrait of Baroness Erzsébet Haller* depicts the daughter of Field Marshal Baron Sámuel Haller holding a brush and palette and beside her on a table with a marble top there is a small paint box. Between 1756 and 1767, Dániel Schmiddely painted a series of 14 portraits of which this is one. Today 12 are extant but the whereabouts of the other two is unknown. All of similar dimensions and compositional organisation, the paintings represent aristocratic young women and recognise contemporary requirements of high society manners and etiquette. The girls are depicted painting, drawing, playing the piano, standing by a globe or arranging a bouquet in a Rococo vase. These portraits, while seen as examples of a new representative genre, also bear witness to the artistic and intellectual education aristocratic society required from young aristocratic women at the time, hence they are depicted in the process of appropriating this education. The series, produced for the Convent of the Sisters of Notre Dame in Pozsony (Bratislava), represents the school's pupils in blue uniform. The religious order of Lorraine, under which this school operated, began its activity in the area in 1748 under temporary conditions. Schmiddely's paintings probably furnished the college and school that was finally built in 1754.  
Schmiddely studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna. He then lived and worked in Pozsony (Bratislava) where he also undertook official commissions, and according to records, he was a professor of drawing at a college there. In view of this series of paintings, the college he worked at was that of the Sisters of Notre Dame.
fac6052d-8778-5973-8864-63b61123c63f.short_description: Schmiddely was a tutor in painting and drawing in Pozsony (Bratislava). The Portrait *of Baroness Erzsébet Haller* is part of a series of 14 portraits, others of which are in Slovakia and Bohemia. The paintings, depicting young women dressed in blue uniforms, refer to different aspects of a good education.

fb4db280-b1e8-5792-9924-ea1569ecf8e4.name: *Petar II Anton Hilleprand-Prandau*
fb4db280-b1e8-5792-9924-ea1569ecf8e4.description:
Baron Petar II Anton Hilleprand-Prandau stands at the centre of the painting finely dressed and wearing a long wig. His left arm rests on a marble-topped table, while his right arm points to the manor house he had built in the background. The family crest is in the right upper corner.  
Petar II was one of the most respected members of this distinguished family originally from Tyrol. He was born in Bozen, studied law in Ingolstadt and served with the Austrian Court. Granted the Valpovo estate in Slavonia in 1721, he died in Vienna in 1771.  
Commissioned to mark a double jubilee, the painting celebrates the Baron's 75th birthday, and commemorates the right of the female line of the family to inherit the Valpovo estate.  
Although much about the life and work of Hochhauser remains a mystery, we do know that he studied at the Vienna Academy under Jacob van Schuppen. We know that the court painter and favourite of Empress Maria Theresia, Martin van Meytens, was a great influence on him, and that he was well trained and kept to the best portrait traditions of the time, relying on the generally accepted and acknowledged conventions of Baroque portrait painting.
fb4db280-b1e8-5792-9924-ea1569ecf8e4.short_description: A portrait of Baron Petar II Anton Hilleprand-Prandau, painted by Ephraim Hochhauser who studied painting at the Vienna Academy under Jacob van Schuppen. In his portraits, Hochhauser relies on the generally accepted and recognised conventions of Baroque portrait painting. Influenced by Martin van Meytens, court painter and favourite of Empress Maria Theresia.

fba06fef-805f-5de9-8213-221cfe8fe3db.name: Nephrite bowl with enamel picture
fba06fef-805f-5de9-8213-221cfe8fe3db.short_description: This bowl features the enamelled portrait of Fath-Ali Shah Qajar, emperor of Persia (AD 1797–1834); it is signed by the artist, Ghülam Khanetzad, and dated AH 1233. Until his death in AD 1834, Fath-Ali Shah Qajar hoped to forge an alliance between Persia and Austria. This bowl was probably sent to Emperor Franz I in Vienna in connection with these efforts.

fc0202a4-85ca-5193-af7d-ee6857a9426b.name: Arabi, Sayed Ahmed Pasha (1841–1911), Colonel Ali Fahmi Bey, Colonel Abdellal Hilmi Bey
fc0202a4-85ca-5193-af7d-ee6857a9426b.short_description: Portrait of minister Arabi (Urabi) together with two officers. In 1882, the war minister took power in Egypt and demanded an end to the financial control imposed by the UK and France. This led to an intervention by the British Navy under Admiral Seymour, who defeated the Egyptian army.

fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.name: Portrait of the Marquess of Cerralbo in a Turkish Garment
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, marquise of Cerralbo, shows the playful and aesthetic use of typical Turkish costume in the Abdullah Frères studio, perfect to satisfy the European desire of exoticism.

keywords: Portrait; women; souvenir; memorabilia; orientalism

feb66ca9-ced9-518b-8f58-1ac129aebdd4.short_description: Portrait of Lazar Sozich. He was a commander of Herzegovinian freedom fighters against the Turks in 1876. This insurrection against the Turks provoked the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which led to the occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Austrian Empire.
